Il nucleo è la collezione del chirurgo e anatomista settecentesco John Hunter, ampliata con preparati anatomici e patologici, strumenti chirurgici, modelli e opere d’arte. Le gallerie seguono scienza, tecnica ed etica della chirurgia dalle pratiche antiche alle sale operatorie moderne, mostrando come osservazione e collezionismo abbiano trasformato la medicina.

Founded as the Imperial War Museum in 1917, it was intended to record the civil and military war effort and sacrifice of the United Kingdom and its Empire during the First World War.

Composed of the Materials Library and the MakeSpace, its work focuses on hands-on research into materials and making from many different perspectives. Members are encouraged to "make, break, design and combine both advanced and traditional tools, techniques and materials".

places.name: Jewel Tower
places.description: The Jewel Tower is a 14th-century surviving element of the Palace of Westminster, in London, England. It was built between 1365 and 1366, under the direction of William of Sleaford and Henry de Yevele, to house the personal treasure of King Edward III. The original tower was a three-storey, crenellated stone building which occupied a secluded part of the palace and was protected by a moat linked to the River Thames.

Fu costruita tra il 1365 e il 1366, sotto la direzione di Guglielmo di Sleaford e Enrico di Yevele, per ospitare il tesoro personale del re Edoardo III. La torre originale era un edificio in pietra a tre piani che occupava una parte appartata del palazzo ed era protetto da un fossato legato al Tamigi.

The events, programmes and activities at the museum aim to provoke questions, challenge prejudice, and encourage understanding.

The building was originally a pair of semi-detached houses known as "Wentworth Place".

Its huge hydraulic machine, bearing the motto ‘Facts not Opinions’, pulled and crushed full-size samples so engineers could understand the strength of iron, steel and structures.

places.name: Lesnes Abbey
places.description: Lesnes Abbey is a former abbey, now ruined, in Abbey Wood, in the London Borough of Bexley, south-east London, England. It is a scheduled monument, and the abbey's ruins are listed at Grade II by Historic England. The adjacent Lesnes Abbey Woods are a Local Nature Reserve. Part of the wood is the Abbey Wood SSSI, a geological Site of Special Scientific Interest which is an important site for fossils of the early Tertiary period.

Parte del bosco è l'Abbazia Wood SSSI, un sito geologico di interesse scientifico speciale che è un importante sito per i fossili del primo periodo terziario.

places.name: Little Holland House
places.description: Little Holland House in Carshalton was built between 1902 and 1904 by artist and designer Frank Dickinson as his family home. Inspired by William Morris and the Arts and Crafts movement, Dickinson designed much of the house himself and filled it with hand-painted decoration, carved furniture, metalwork, textiles and pictures. Preserved largely as the family left it, the modest suburban interior shows how Arts and Crafts ideals could shape an entire everyday home.

Conservato in gran parte come lo lasciò la famiglia, l’interno mostra come quegli ideali potessero modellare un’intera casa quotidiana.

Situated on the site of the old Kew Bridge Pumping Station in Brentford, near Kew Bridge on the River Thames in West London, England, the museum is centred on a collection of stationary water pumping steam engines dating from 1820 to 1910.

The museum predominantly hosts exhibits relating to the heritage of London's transport, as well as conserving and explaining the history of it. The majority of the museum's exhibits originated in the collections of London Transport, but, since the creation of Transport for London (TfL) in 2000, the remit of the museum has expanded to cover all aspects of transport in the city and in some instances beyond.

La maggior parte delle mostre del museo ha avuto origine nelle collezioni di London Transport, ma, dalla creazione di Transport for London (TfL) nel 2000, il remit del museo si è ampliato per coprire tutti gli aspetti del trasporto in città e in alcuni casi oltre.

places.description: London’s Roman Amphitheatre lies beneath Guildhall Art Gallery, where dark stone outlines at street level mark the arena’s position. Excavated walls, drains and timber remains reveal the venue built for public spectacles in Roman Londinium, interpreted in a free underground display.

places.name: Marble Hill
places.description: Marble Hill House is a Neo-Palladian villa, now Grade I listed, in Twickenham in the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames. It was built between 1724 and 1729 as the home of Henrietta Howard, Countess of Suffolk, who lived there until her death. The compact design soon became famous and furnished a standard model for the Georgian English villa and for plantation houses in the American colonies.

Il design compatto divenne presto famoso e arredato un modello standard per la villa inglese georgiana e per le case di piantagioni nelle colonie americane.

places.description: The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) is an English cricket club founded in 1787, whose Lord's headquarters are dubbed "the Home of Cricket". Lord's Cricket Ground has been owned since Victorian times by MCC, which served as cricket's governing body from 1788 to 1909 and retains considerable global influence.

places.name: Museum of Croydon
places.description: The Museum of Croydon is a museum located within the Croydon Clocktower arts facility in Central Croydon, England. It showcases historical and cultural artefacts relating to the London Borough of Croydon and its people. The museum is owned and run by Croydon Council. It is located on the upper ground floor of Croydon Clocktower, but also incorporates the Riesco Gallery, on the lower ground floor, which displays Roman and Anglo-Saxon collections and a collection of Chinese ceramics.

Si trova al piano terra superiore di Croydon Clocktower, ma incorpora anche la Galleria Riesco, al piano terra inferiore, che mostra collezioni romane e anglosassone e una collezione di ceramiche cinesi.

places.description: London Museum Docklands occupies a Georgian warehouse at West India Quay and tells the history of the Thames, the port and East London. Galleries address Roman trade, docks and warehouses, migration, wartime destruction and the legacies of slavery, including an atmospheric reconstruction of nineteenth-century Sailortown.

places.description: The Museum of the Home explores how domestic life has evolved over the centuries. Step into Rooms Through Time to see changing interiors, wander the Home Galleries to reflect on everyday life, and stroll the Gardens Through Time, which mirror shifts in society and style. With exhibitions, family days, and festivals, it’s a lively place to discover the past—and rethink the present.

Con mostre, giornate di famiglia e festival, è un luogo vivace per scoprire il passato e ripensare il presente.

Friendly volunteers, hands‑on displays and a small shop make it an engaging, accessible stop for history and medical heritage fans

places.description: The National Army Museum is the national home of the history and heritage of the Army. Through permanent galleries, special exhibitions, collections and programmes, the museum explores how soldiers have shaped our world and lives, from the British Civil Wars to the Army's role today. places.description: The National Maritime Museum (NMM) is a maritime museum in Greenwich, London. It is part of Royal Museums Greenwich, a network of museums in the Maritime Greenwich World Heritage Site. Like other publicly funded national museums in the United Kingdom, it has no general admission charge; there are admission charges for most side-gallery temporary exhibitions, usually supplemented by many loaned works from other museums.

places.name: National Portrait Gallery
places.description: London’s National Portrait Gallery tells British history through portraits of the people who shaped it, from Tudor monarchs and writers to scientists, performers and contemporary public figures. More than 11,000 paintings, drawings, miniatures and sculptures form the Primary Collection, complemented by extensive photography and works on paper; the chronological galleries make changing ideas of identity, power and celebrity easy to follow.
places.descriptionIt: La National Portrait Gallery di Londra racconta la storia britannica attraverso i ritratti delle persone che l’hanno plasmata, dai sovrani Tudor e dagli scrittori fino a scienziati, artisti e protagonisti contemporanei. La collezione principale comprende oltre 11.000 dipinti, disegni, miniature e sculture, affiancati da vaste raccolte fotografiche e opere su carta; le sale cronologiche mostrano con chiarezza l’evoluzione di identità, potere e celebrità.

places.name: National Trust - Eastbury Manor House
places.description: Eastbury Manor House is a Grade I listed building situated in the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham in Greater London, England. It dates to the Elizabethan period, although the land on which it was built was formerly part of the demesne of Barking Abbey. The house is owned by the National Trust but has been managed since the 1930s by the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham and its predecessors.

Esso risale al periodo elisabettiano, anche se la terra su cui è stato costruito era precedentemente parte del demisno dell'Abbazia di Barking. La casa è di proprietà del National Trust ma è stata gestita dagli anni '30 dal London Borough di Barking e Dagenham e dai suoi predecessori.

places.name: Queen's House
places.description: Queen's House is a former royal residence in the London borough of Greenwich, which presently serves as a public art gallery. It was built between 1616 and 1635 on the grounds of the now demolished Greenwich Palace, a few miles downriver from the City of London. In its current setting, it forms a central focus of the Old Royal Naval College with a grand vista leading to the River Thames, a World Heritage Site called Maritime Greenwich.
places.descriptionIt: Queen's House è un'ex residenza reale nel quartiere di Londra di Greenwich, che attualmente funge da galleria d'arte pubblica. Fu costruito tra il 1616 e il 1635 sul terreno dell'ormai demolita Greenwich Palace, a pochi chilometri di distanza dalla città di Londra. Nella sua impostazione attuale, forma un centro centrale del vecchio Royal Naval College con un grande vista che conduce al Tamigi, un patrimonio mondiale chiamato Maritime Greenwich.

places.name: Royal Academy of Music
places.description: The Royal Academy of Music (RAM) in Westminster, London, England, is one of the oldest music schools in the United Kingdom, founded in 1822 by John Fane and Nicolas-Charles Bochsa. It received its royal charter in 1830 from King George IV with the support of the first Duke of Wellington. The academy provides undergraduate and postgraduate training across instrumental performance, composition, jazz, musical theatre and opera, and recruits musicians from around the world, with a student community representing more than 50 nationalities.
places.descriptionIt: La Royal Academy of Music (RAM) di Westminster, Londra, Inghilterra, è una delle più antiche scuole di musica del Regno Unito, fondata nel 1822 da John Fane e Nicolas-Charles Bochsa. Ricevette la sua carta reale nel 1830 da re Giorgio IV con il sostegno del primo duca di Wellington. L'accademia fornisce formazione universitaria e post-laurea attraverso performance strumentali, composizione, jazz, teatro musicale e opera, e recluta musicisti da tutto il mondo, con una comunità studentesca che rappresenta più di 50 nazionalità.

places.description: The Royal Air Force Museum London (also commonly known as the RAF Museum) is located on the former Hendon Aerodrome, in North London's Borough of Barnet. It includes five buildings and hangars showing the history of aviation and the Royal Air Force. It is part of the Royal Air Force Museum. There is another site at Royal Air Force Museum Midlands at RAF Cosford in Shropshire.

places.description: The Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) is a professional body for architects primarily in the United Kingdom, but also internationally, founded for the advancement of architecture under its royal charter granted in 1837, three supplemental charters and a new charter granted in 1971. Founded as the Institute of British Architects in London in 1834, RIBA has a central London office (temporarily moved from 66 Portland Place from mid-2025 due to building refurbishment work) as well as a network of regional offices.

places.description: The RSA Interpretation Centre preserves the history of the Royal Small Arms Factory at Enfield Lock beneath the former factory clock tower. Oral histories, archival material and industrial objects explain weapons manufacture and the lives of employees; access is generally by arrangement or during announced community open days.

places.name: Saatchi Gallery
places.description: The Saatchi Gallery is a London gallery for contemporary art and an independent charity opened by Charles Saatchi in 1985. Exhibitions which drew upon the collection of Charles Saatchi, starting with US artists and minimalism, moving to the Damien Hirst-led Young British Artists, followed by shows purely of painting, led to Saatchi Gallery becoming a recognised authority in contemporary art globally.

places.name: Sambourne House
places.description: Sambourne House, previously known as 18 Stafford Terrace and Linley Sambourne House, was the home of the Punch illustrator Edward Linley Sambourne (1844–1910) in Kensington, London. The house, now Grade II* listed, is currently open to the public as a museum. In 1875 when the Sambournes moved in, 18 Stafford Terrace was an almost new townhouse.

La casa, ora classificata Grade II*, è attualmente aperta al pubblico come museo. Nel 1875 quando i Sambournes si trasferirono, 18 Stafford Terrace era una casa di città quasi nuova.

places.name: Science Gallery London
places.description: Science Gallery London operated at King’s College London’s Guy’s Campus from 2018 until its permanent closure on 1 August 2026. In the restored Boland House opposite London Bridge, its free thematic seasons brought artists, researchers, students and local communities together through exhibitions, performances, experiments and discussions about art, science and health. The gallery programme has ended, although parts of Boland House remain in use.

Nella restaurata Boland House, di fronte a London Bridge, le stagioni tematiche gratuite riunivano artisti, ricercatori, studenti e comunità locali con mostre, performance, esperimenti e dibattiti su arte, scienza e salute. Il programma della galleria è terminato, anche se parti di Boland House restano in uso.

places.description: London’s Science Museum explores how scientific ideas and technologies changed everyday life through landmark objects, working models and interactive galleries. Highlights range from full-size steam engines and historic aircraft to space hardware, communications technology and the vast Medicine galleries; Wonderlab adds hands-on experiments and live demonstrations for families.

Il percorso spazia da grandi motori a vapore e aerei storici fino a veicoli spaziali, telecomunicazioni e vaste gallerie dedicate alla medicina; Wonderlab aggiunge esperimenti pratici e dimostrazioni dal vivo per le famiglie.

places.name: Sir John Soane's Museum
places.description: Sir John Soane’s Museum in Lincoln’s Inn Fields is the house-museum of the neoclassical architect Sir John Soane. Founded in 1837, the museum has been preserved exactly as Soane left it at the time of his death, with a vast collection of over 45,000 objects, including architectural drawings, models, paintings, sculptures, and antiquities. The museum is renowned for its unique and fascinating atmosphere, with narrow rooms and passages decorated with Soane’s collections. Some of the most notable pieces include works by Canaletto, Turner, Hogarth, and Joshua Reynolds
places.descriptionIt: Il museo di Sir John Soane in Lincoln’s Inn Fields è la casa-museo dell’architetto neoclassico Sir John Soane. Fondato nel 1837, il museo è stato conservato esattamente come Soane l'ha lasciata al momento della sua morte, con una vasta collezione di oltre 45.000 oggetti, tra cui disegni architettonici, modelli, dipinti, sculture e antichità. Il museo è rinomato per la sua atmosfera unica e affascinante, con stanze strette e passaggi decorati con le collezioni di Soane. Alcuni dei pezzi più importanti includono opere di Canaletto, Turner, Hogarth e Joshua Reynolds

The Georgian era quadrangle is built on the site of a Tudor palace ("Old Somerset House") originally belonging to Edward Seymour, 1st Duke of Somerset.

Il quadrango di epoca georgiano è costruito sul sito di un palazzo di Tudor ("Casa Vecchia Somerset") originariamente appartenente a Edward Seymour, I duca di Somerset.

places.description: Thames River Police Museum is housed at Wapping Police Station, near the base from which the Marine Police began patrolling in 1798. Uniforms, equipment, photographs and case histories trace the world’s oldest continuously operating police force and the changing work of policing the river.

places.description: The British Dental Museum holds the British Dental Association’s collection of instruments, furniture, photographs and archives. Displays chart the development of dentistry from painful extraction and handmade dentures to anaesthesia, preventive care and modern professional training; visits normally require advance arrangement.

places.name: The British Library
places.description: The British Library is the national library of the United Kingdom. Based in London, it is one of the largest libraries in the world, with an estimated collection of over 200 million items from multiple countries. As a legal deposit library, it receives copies of all books produced in the United Kingdom and Ireland, as well as a significant proportion of overseas titles distributed in the United Kingdom.
places.descriptionIt: La British Library è la biblioteca nazionale del Regno Unito. Con sede a Londra, è una delle più grandi biblioteche del mondo, con una raccolta stimata di oltre 200 milioni di articoli provenienti da più paesi. Come biblioteca legale, riceve copie di tutti i libri prodotti nel Regno Unito e in Irlanda, nonché una percentuale significativa di titoli all'estero distribuiti nel Regno Unito.

places.hook: The British Library is the national library of the United Kingdom. Based in London, it is one of the largest libraries in the world, with an estimated collection of over 200 million items from multiple countries.
places.hookIt: La British Library è la biblioteca nazionale del Regno Unito. Con sede a Londra, è una delle più grandi biblioteche del mondo, con una raccolta stimata di oltre 200 milioni di articoli provenienti da più paesi.

places.name: The British Museum
places.description: The British Museum is a public museum dedicated to human history, art and culture located in the Bloomsbury area of London. Its permanent collection of eight million artefacts is the largest in the world. It documents the story of human culture from its beginnings to the present. Established in 1753, the British Museum was the world's first public national museum.
places.descriptionIt: Il British Museum è un museo pubblico dedicato alla storia, all'arte e alla cultura umana situato nella zona di Bloomsbury a Londra. La sua collezione permanente di otto milioni di manufatti è la più grande al mondo. Documenta la storia della cultura umana dai suoi inizi al presente. Fondato nel 1753, il British Museum è stato il primo museo pubblico nazionale al mondo.

places.name: The Cartoon Museum
places.description: Cartoon Museum is a cosy, friendly spot celebrating British cartoon, comic and caricature art. Exhibitions display original strips, political cartoons and illustration; workshops, family activities and talks bring creativity to life. A welcoming shop, rotating displays and knowledgeable staff make it ideal for curious visitors and families. Compact galleries reward a relaxed visit; check opening times for special events and workshops. Guided tours and family trails add extra fun and insight also.

Mostre mostrano strisce originali, cartoni animati politici e illustrazione; workshop, attività familiari e colloqui portano alla vita la creatività. Un negozio accogliente, display rotanti e personale competente lo rendono ideale per visitatori e famiglie curiosi. Le gallerie compatte premiano una visita rilassata; verificano i tempi di apertura per eventi speciali e workshop. Visite guidate e percorsi familiari aggiungono divertimento e intuizioni extra.

places.name: The Charterhouse
places.description: Charterhouse is a serene, historic complex in Clerkenwell tracing 650 years from a 14th‑century Carthusian priory to a Tudor mansion, school and still‑working almshouse. Guided tours reveal cloisters, grand rooms, a chapel, peaceful courtyards and gardens; volunteers share vivid stories of residents, founders and reform. Tucked by Charterhouse Square near the Barbican, it’s a quietly moving stop for history lovers

Visite guidate rivelano chiostri, grandi camere, una cappella, cortili pacifici e giardini; i volontari condividono storie vivide di residenti, fondatori e riforma. Incastonato da Charterhouse Square vicino al Barbican, è una tappa tranquilla per gli amanti della storia

Screenings and guided events recreate the culture of picture palaces and filmgoing, but access is normally tied to booked tours or programmed events.

places.description: The City of London Police Museum was a museum housed at the Guildhall, City of London. It treated the history of the City of London Police. Exhibits included uniforms, Victorian-era police equipment and artefacts, communication devices, World War II displays, and exhibits about Jack the Ripper and other famous murder cases.

Le esposizioni includevano uniformi, attrezzature e artefatti della polizia di epoca vittoriana, dispositivi di comunicazione, esposizioni della seconda guerra mondiale, e mostre su Jack lo Squartatore e altri famosi casi di omicidio.

places.description: Foundling Museum in Bloomsbury tells the moving story of Britain’s first children’s charity and the Foundling Hospital. Galleries display Hogarth and Handel connections, social history, portraits and decorative arts alongside personal objects and archives. Evocative rooms, family trails, talks and temporary exhibitions bring lives and reform to life. A welcoming shop and café make it a thoughtful, accessible stop for curious visitors

Gallerie espongono connessioni Hogarth e Handel, storia sociale, ritratti e arti decorative insieme oggetti personali e archivi. Sale evocative, percorsi familiari, colloqui e mostre temporanee portano vita e riforma alla vita. Un accogliente negozio e caffè lo rendono una sosta piacevole e accessibile per i visitatori curiosi

places.description: The Langdon Down Centre preserves Normansfield, the institution founded in 1868 by physician John Langdon Down and his wife Mary for people with learning disabilities. The museum and ornate Victorian theatre document changing care, education and attitudes, including Down’s influential and contested medical legacy.

places.description: The Mosaic Rooms is a non-profit gallery in a converted Kensington townhouse devoted to modern and contemporary culture from the Arab world and beyond. places.description: The Musical Museum in Brentford houses self-playing musical instruments ranging from tiny music boxes to reproducing pianos and a powerful Wurlitzer theatre organ. Demonstrations reveal how paper rolls, pinned barrels, pneumatics and early electrical systems brought mechanically performed music into homes and cinemas.

places.description: The National Archives in Kew houses over a thousand years of British history in a modern, visitor-friendly building. Browse free exhibitions, consult original documents in the reading rooms with a reader’s ticket, enjoy talks and family activities, and relax in the café and shop. Helpful staff and regular events make it ideal for researchers, history fans and curious visitors; allow a few hours to explore. places.description: The Old Operating Theatre Museum occupies an eighteenth-century church attic above the former St Thomas’ Hospital. Its surviving 1822 surgical theatre and herb garret reveal pre-anaesthetic operations, medical teaching and the preparation of remedies in one of Europe’s oldest operating-theatre interiors.

Free exhibitions draw on survivor testimony, photographs, documents and books collected since the 1930s, while its reading room supports deeper research into genocide and displacement.

Exhibitions connect those recordings with the estate’s earlier social history and the specialist teams who analysed them.

Le esposizioni collegano quelle registrazioni con la storia sociale precedente della tenuta e le squadre specializzate che le hanno analizzate.

places.description: Two Temple Place is a jewel-like neo-Gothic mansion on the Embankment, built in 1895 by William Waldorf Astor. Its lavish stonework, carved wood, stained glass and ornate interiors host rotating exhibitions and cultural events. Guided tours reveal hidden details and dramatic rooms. Tucked between Temple and the river, it's a surprising, intimate stop for architecture lovers and curious visitors. Check opening times for exhibitions, talks and events; nearby cafés, riverside are ideal for lingering.

Incastonato tra il Tempio e il fiume, è una sorprendente, intima fermata per gli amanti dell'architettura e visitatori curiosi. places.description: The Vagina Museum is the world's first brick and mortar museum about the female reproductive system. The project is based in the United Kingdom, and moved into its first fixed location in Camden Market, London, in October 2019. Its first exhibition opened on 16 November 2019. It moved to its second premises in Bethnal Green in March 2022 where it remained until February 2023.

places.description: The V&A at South Kensington grew from the Museum of Manufactures founded after the Great Exhibition of 1851. Its vast purpose-built complex holds decorative arts and design from many cultures, including ceramics, fashion, furniture, jewellery, metalwork, photography and sculpture. Highlights such as the Cast Courts, Raphael Cartoons and British Galleries make the building itself part of the story of Victorian design education.

Spazi come le Cast Courts, i cartoni di Raffaello e le British Galleries rendono l’edificio stesso parte della storia dell’educazione al design nell’età vittoriana.

places.description: Wandle Industrial Museum explains the industries powered by the River Wandle, once one of Britain’s hardest-working rivers. Displays cover textile printing, snuff, flour, leather and the firms associated with William Morris and Liberty, using tools, samples, maps and local workers’ stories.

places.name: Wellcome Collection
places.description: The Wellcome Collection is a unique museum that explores the connection between medicine, art, and life. Founded by Sir Henry Wellcome, a philanthropist and collector passionate about medical history, it hosts a wide range of exhibitions. You'll find everything from ancient medical equipment to contemporary artworks that reflect themes of health and well-being. The museum is known for its interactive and provocative exhibits that stimulate curiosity and dialogue about what it means to be human. It has an excellent café, a large and rich shop, and an amazing reading room where you can spend some time relaxing
places.descriptionIt: La Wellcome Collection è un museo unico che esplora il legame tra medicina, arte e vita. Fondata da Sir Henry Wellcome, un filantropo e collezionista appassionato di storia medica, ospita una vasta gamma di mostre. Troverete tutto, dalle antiche attrezzature mediche alle opere d'arte contemporanee che riflettono temi di salute e benessere. Il museo è noto per le sue esposizioni interattive e provocatorie che stimolano la curiosità e il dialogo su ciò che significa essere umani. Ha un ottimo caffè, un grande e ricco negozio, e una straordinaria sala lettura dove trascorrere un po 'di tempo rilassante

The Museum of Methodism in the chapel crypt uses portraits, objects and archives to trace Wesley, preaching, social reform and the movement’s international growth.

places.description: This White Cube pin is the Bermondsey gallery, opened in 2011 in a converted 1970s warehouse on Bermondsey Street. A sequence of large, spare exhibition rooms—including a tall central gallery suited to sculpture and installations—supports ambitious solo shows and historically framed group exhibitions. The building also contains viewing rooms, an auditorium and an archive, making it the gallery’s substantial South London base rather than a reference to its overseas branches.

Una sequenza di grandi sale essenziali, compreso uno spazio centrale alto adatto a sculture e installazioni, ospita ambiziose personali e collettive di taglio storico. L’edificio comprende anche viewing rooms, auditorium e archivio: è la grande sede nel sud di Londra, non un riferimento alle filiali estere.

places.name: Whitehall
places.description: Whitehall in Cheam is a timber-framed historic house whose earliest fabric dates from about 1500, not the government street in Westminster. Successive occupants enlarged and refitted it, leaving rooms with Tudor structure and Georgian, Victorian and Edwardian details. Displays explore the Killick family, Cheam’s local history and nearby Nonsuch Palace, while the garden preserves a medieval well associated with an earlier building.
places.descriptionIt: Whitehall a Cheam è una casa storica a graticcio, con le parti più antiche risalenti circa al 1500: non è la strada governativa di Westminster. Gli abitanti successivi la ampliarono e trasformarono, lasciando struttura Tudor e dettagli georgiani, vittoriani ed edoardiani. Le sale raccontano la famiglia Killick, la storia di Cheam e il vicino Nonsuch Palace; nel giardino resta un pozzo medievale legato a un edificio precedente.

places.description: William Morris Gallery in Walthamstow sits in Water House, a Grade II* Georgian villa set in Lloyd Park. Home to the world’s largest public collection of Morris’s designs, it celebrates his Arts and Crafts legacy with displays, workshops and changing exhibitions. Free to enter, the gallery offers family activities, a shop and a peaceful park setting—ideal for design lovers and curious visitors.

Casa della più grande collezione pubblica mondiale di disegni di Morris, celebra il suo patrimonio di arti e mestieri con esposizioni, workshop e mostre mutevoli. Libero di entrare, la galleria offre attività familiari, un negozio e un parco tranquillo, ideale per gli amanti del design e i visitatori curiosi.

Maps, paintings, photographs, archaeology and domestic objects highlight local people, buildings and industries beyond the famous tennis championships.

places.name: Wimbledon Windmill Museum
places.description: Wimbledon Windmill Museum sits atop Wimbledon Common in a charming 1817 windmill. Free to enter on open days, it showcases milling history, working models and local stories, plus displays on the Scouting movement. Climb narrow stairs for views, watch the sails turn on special weekends, enjoy hands-on exhibits for children and a cosy tearoom nearby. A delightful, family-friendly stop amid wide commons and woodland walks. Open weekends; check sail-turning times and book guided tours in advance!
places.descriptionIt: Wimbledon Windmill Museum si trova in cima a Wimbledon Common in un affascinante mulino a vento del 1817. Libero di entrare nei giorni aperti, mostra storia di fresatura, modelli di lavoro e storie locali, oltre a esposizioni sul movimento scouting. Salire scale strette per la vista, guardare le vele girano nei weekend speciali, godere di esposizioni hands-on per i bambini e una accogliente sala da tè nelle vicinanze. Una deliziosa e familiare fermata tra ampi comuni e passeggiate nel bosco. Aprire i fine settimana; controllare i tempi di navigazione e prenotare visite guidate in anticipo!

places.description: Singer Amy Winehouse lived and died at this Camden Square house in 2011. The building remains a private residence, while the address has become an informal place of remembrance connected to her distinctive voice, troubled public life and deep association with Camden.

L’edificio resta un’abitazione privata, mentre l’indirizzo è diventato un luogo informale della memoria legato alla sua voce inconfondibile, alla difficile vita pubblica e al forte rapporto con Camden.

places.name: 31 Gordon Sq
places.description: No. 31 Gordon Square formed part of Bloomsbury’s network of homes associated with writers, artists and reformers. The square’s restrained Georgian façades conceal the intense intellectual and personal exchanges of the Bloomsbury Group; identify the exact plaque on site rather than treating the whole terrace as one house.
places.descriptionIt: Il numero 31 di Gordon Square faceva parte della rete di case frequentate da scrittori, artisti e riformatori di Bloomsbury. Le sobrie facciate georgiane nascondono gli intensi scambi intellettuali e personali del Bloomsbury Group; conviene leggere la targa esatta sul posto invece di considerare l’intera terrazza come un’unica casa.

places.name: 67 Hopton St
places.description: This Hopton Street house is one of the small surviving domestic buildings tucked behind Tate Modern and the former Bankside power station. Its scale records the older residential fabric of Southwark, now surrounded by converted industrial buildings and major cultural institutions.
places.descriptionIt: Questa casa di Hopton Street è uno dei piccoli edifici domestici sopravvissuti dietro Tate Modern e l’ex centrale di Bankside. Le sue dimensioni testimoniano il tessuto residenziale più antico di Southwark, oggi circondato da edifici industriali riconvertiti e grandi istituzioni culturali.

places.name: Abbey Mills Pumping Station
places.description: Abbey Mills Pumping Station was designed by Joseph Bazalgette’s engineers in the 1860s as part of London’s new sewer system. Its lavish Byzantine-inspired towers and polychrome brickwork earned it the nickname ‘Cathedral of Sewage’, disguising heavy pumping machinery within an exceptionally ornate industrial monument.
places.descriptionIt: Abbey Mills Pumping Station fu progettata dagli ingegneri di Joseph Bazalgette negli anni Sessanta dell’Ottocento per il nuovo sistema fognario londinese. Torri d’ispirazione bizantina e mattoni policromi le valsero il soprannome di “Cattedrale delle Fogne”, celando grandi macchinari in un monumento industriale eccezionalmente ornato.

places.name: Abbey Rd crossing
places.description: The zebra crossing outside Abbey Road Studios became one of music’s most imitated images after appearing on the Beatles’ 1969 album cover. It remains a working road crossing, not a film set, and visitors should use it normally without stopping traffic or blocking residents.
places.descriptionIt: Le strisce pedonali davanti agli Abbey Road Studios divennero una delle immagini musicali più imitate dopo la copertina dell’album dei Beatles del 1969. Restano un attraversamento stradale in uso, non un set: vanno utilizzate normalmente senza fermare il traffico o intralciare i residenti.

places.description: Agatha Christie lived in this Chelsea house during a productive period of her career. The blue plaque turns a private stucco façade into a precise literary landmark connected to the creator of Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple; the interior is not a visitor attraction.

places.name: Aldgate Pump
places.description: Aldgate Pump marks an old water source at the eastern edge of the City. Its present cast-iron form dates from the nineteenth century, and the wolf’s-head spout recalls the last wolf said to have been killed nearby; contaminated water from the pump also became notorious in Victorian health investigations.
places.descriptionIt: Aldgate Pump indica un’antica fonte d’acqua al margine orientale della City. L’attuale struttura in ghisa è ottocentesca e il beccuccio a testa di lupo ricorda l’ultimo lupo che si dice ucciso nei dintorni; l’acqua contaminata della pompa divenne inoltre nota nelle indagini sanitarie vittoriane.

places.name: Annabel's
places.description: Annabel’s is a private members’ club founded by Mark Birley in 1963 and now housed in a richly decorated Berkeley Square townhouse. Its changing floral façades are public spectacles, but the theatrical interiors, restaurants and nightclub remain accessible only to members and their guests.
places.descriptionIt: Annabel’s è un club privato fondato da Mark Birley nel 1963 e oggi ospitato in una townhouse riccamente decorata di Berkeley Square. Le installazioni floreali sulla facciata sono spettacoli pubblici, ma gli interni teatrali, i ristoranti e il nightclub restano riservati ai soci e ai loro ospiti.

places.name: ArcelorMittal Orbit
places.description: Anish Kapoor and Cecil Balmond’s ArcelorMittal Orbit was built for the 2012 Olympic Park as a looping red-steel observation tower. Its deliberately unstable-looking structure contains viewing platforms and the later-added tunnel slide, combining public art, engineering and an unconventional visitor ride.
places.descriptionIt: L’ArcelorMittal Orbit di Anish Kapoor e Cecil Balmond fu costruito per il Parco Olimpico del 2012 come torre panoramica di acciaio rosso avvolto su se stesso. La struttura volutamente instabile contiene piattaforme e il successivo scivolo a tunnel, unendo arte pubblica, ingegneria e attrazione.

places.name: Babylon Park London
places.description: Babylon Park is an underground, space-themed amusement arcade beneath Camden Market. Neon planets, rides, games and soft-play areas create a deliberately immersive interior for families; it is a commercial entertainment venue rather than a historic oddity, and entry arrangements vary by activity.

Pianeti al neon, giostre, giochi e aree morbide creano un interno volutamente immersivo per famiglie; è un locale commerciale, non una curiosità storica, e le modalità d’ingresso variano secondo l’attività.

places.name: Bacherozzo
places.description: Bacherozzo is the affectionate local nickname attached to a large insect-like sculpture near Fitzrovia. Its enlarged body and legs turn an easily overlooked urban corner into a surreal encounter; inspect the work itself for artist and title information rather than assuming it depicts a specific species.
places.descriptionIt: Bacherozzo è il soprannome affettuoso dato a una grande scultura simile a un insetto vicino a Fitzrovia. Corpo e zampe ingranditi trasformano un angolo urbano facile da ignorare in un incontro surreale; conviene leggere sul posto autore e titolo senza attribuirle una specie precisa.

places.name: Banksy Basquiat
places.description: Banksy’s 2017 mural near the Barbican responds to Jean-Michel Basquiat’s exhibition with a crowned figure being searched by police. The stencil deliberately collides Basquiat’s visual language with surveillance and institutional approval, and survives as a protected street artwork near the cultural complex.
places.descriptionIt: Il murale di Banksy del 2017 vicino al Barbican risponde alla mostra di Jean-Michel Basquiat con una figura incoronata perquisita dalla polizia. Lo stencil mette volutamente in collisione il linguaggio visivo di Basquiat con sorveglianza e approvazione istituzionale, sopravvivendo come opera di strada protetta.

places.name: Banksy I love London Robbo
places.description: This surviving Banksy work emerged from the long graffiti rivalry between Banksy and London writer King Robbo. Layers of alteration, restoration and commentary make the wall a document of street-art authorship and territorial dispute rather than a pristine single-artist mural.
places.descriptionIt: Quest’opera superstite di Banksy nasce dalla lunga rivalità nel graffiti writing tra Banksy e l’artista londinese King Robbo. Strati di modifiche, restauri e commenti trasformano il muro in un documento su autorialità e territorio nella street art, non in un murale intatto di un solo autore.

places.description: The Barbican Conservatory wraps tropical planting around the concrete fly-tower and backstage structures of the Barbican Centre. More than 1,500 plant species, pools and fish occupy London’s second-largest conservatory, usually opened only on selected dates with timed entry.
places.descriptionIt: Il Barbican Conservatory avvolge di vegetazione tropicale la torre scenica e le strutture di servizio in cemento del Barbican Centre. Oltre 1.500 specie, vasche e pesci occupano la seconda serra più grande di Londra, normalmente aperta soltanto in date selezionate con ingresso a orario.

places.name: Barnet Physic Well
places.description: Barnet Physic Well is a seventeenth-century medicinal spring once promoted for its purging waters and visited by Samuel Pepys. The small well house preserves the source beneath suburban Barnet, but interior access is normally limited to organised openings rather than daily visits.
places.descriptionIt: Barnet Physic Well è una sorgente medicinale seicentesca, un tempo pubblicizzata per le sue acque purgative e visitata da Samuel Pepys. Il piccolo edificio conserva la fonte sotto la Barnet suburbana, ma l’interno è normalmente accessibile solo durante aperture organizzate.

places.name: Beavers
places.description: Beavers have returned to west London through a managed reintroduction project in the Paradise Fields wetlands. Their dams, gnawed trunks and changing water channels are more reliably seen than the nocturnal animals themselves, demonstrating how one species can reshape an urban habitat.
places.descriptionIt: I castori sono tornati nella Londra occidentale grazie a un progetto controllato di reintroduzione nelle zone umide di Paradise Fields. Dighe, tronchi rosicchiati e canali modificati si osservano più facilmente degli animali notturni e mostrano come una sola specie possa trasformare un habitat urbano.

places.name: Big Ben
places.description: Big Ben is properly the nickname of the Great Bell inside Elizabeth Tower, not the tower or clock as a whole. Augustus Pugin designed the clock dials and Gothic detailing for Charles Barry’s Palace of Westminster; tours climb hundreds of steps to the mechanism and belfry.
places.descriptionIt: Big Ben è propriamente il soprannome della Great Bell dentro Elizabeth Tower, non della torre o dell’orologio nel suo complesso. Augustus Pugin progettò quadranti e dettagli gotici per il Palace of Westminster di Charles Barry; le visite salgono centinaia di gradini fino al meccanismo e alla cella campanaria.

places.description: The blue plaque marks the Chelsea home of Bram Stoker, author of Dracula and theatre manager to Henry Irving. It links a conventional nineteenth-century terrace to the professional theatrical world and imaginative sources behind one of literature’s most enduring Gothic figures.

places.description: Bridge Pool is a small tidal or riverside remnant beside the Thames path in Nine Elms, where engineered embankments meet older water infrastructure. Its interest lies in reading the surviving basin and surrounding redevelopment together rather than expecting a conventional ornamental pond.

places.description: Brixton Windmill, also called Ashby’s Mill, was built in 1816 and later adapted to steam-powered milling when surrounding development blocked the wind. Restored machinery and volunteer-led tours explain how flour was produced inside a rare surviving tower mill in inner London.

Macchinari restaurati e visite di volontari spiegano la produzione di farina in un raro mulino a torre sopravvissuto nella Londra interna.

places.description: Brown Hart Gardens is an elevated public terrace built in 1906 over the former Duke Street electricity substation. Its Baroque stone pavilion, vents and raised platform reveal the infrastructure beneath, while later planting and seating turned the roof into an unusual Mayfair garden.

Padiglione barocco, prese d’aria e piattaforma rivelano l’infrastruttura sottostante, mentre piante e sedute aggiunte in seguito hanno trasformato il tetto in un insolito giardino di Mayfair.

places.description: The BT Tower was completed in 1964 as the hub of Britain’s microwave telecommunications network. Its cylindrical form carried aerials above surrounding buildings and its rotating restaurant became a symbol of technological optimism; the tower is being converted to a hotel and is not generally open.

La forma cilindrica portava antenne sopra gli edifici e il ristorante girevole divenne simbolo di ottimismo tecnologico; la torre è in trasformazione alberghiera e non è normalmente aperta.

places.description: Burlington Arcade opened in 1819 as one of London’s earliest covered shopping passages. Uniformed beadles still enforce traditional rules beneath the glazed roof, while the narrow sequence of small luxury shops preserves the scale and controlled atmosphere of a Regency arcade.

places.description: The bust of diarist Samuel Pepys stands near the church and Navy Office district that shaped his working life. It recalls both his eyewitness accounts of Restoration London and his administrative reforms, placing a literary face within the streets he described in extraordinary detail.

Ricorda sia le testimonianze sulla Londra della Restaurazione sia le riforme amministrative, collocando un volto letterario nelle strade descritte con eccezionale precisione.

places.name: Cable Street Mural
places.description: The Cable Street Mural commemorates the 1936 confrontation in which local communities blocked Oswald Mosley’s British Union of Fascists. Painted by several artists from the late 1970s onward, its sweeping battle scene turns the wall of St George’s Town Hall into a monument to organised resistance.
places.descriptionIt: Il Cable Street Mural commemora lo scontro del 1936, quando le comunità locali impedirono il passaggio alla British Union of Fascists di Oswald Mosley. Dipinta da vari artisti dalla fine degli anni Settanta, la grande scena trasforma il muro di St George’s Town Hall in un monumento alla resistenza organizzata.

places.name: Caesar's Camp
places.description: Caesar’s Camp is an Iron Age hillfort earthwork on Wimbledon Common, despite the later name linking it to Julius Caesar. Banks and ditches survive among woodland and paths, offering archaeological evidence of a defended settlement rather than a Roman military camp.
places.descriptionIt: Caesar’s Camp è un terrapieno fortificato dell’età del Ferro su Wimbledon Common, nonostante il nome successivo lo colleghi a Giulio Cesare. Argini e fossati sopravvivono tra bosco e sentieri, offrendo prove archeologiche di un insediamento difeso e non di un campo militare romano.

places.name: Caesar's Well
places.description: Caesar’s Well is a spring near the Iron Age earthworks of Caesar’s Camp on Wimbledon Common. The stone-lined source once supplied local water and later fed a cistern; its Roman-sounding name is folklore rather than evidence of a connection to Julius Caesar.
places.descriptionIt: Caesar’s Well è una sorgente vicino ai terrapieni dell’età del Ferro di Caesar’s Camp su Wimbledon Common. La fonte rivestita in pietra forniva acqua locale e in seguito alimentò una cisterna; il nome romano appartiene alla leggenda, non prova un legame con Giulio Cesare.

places.name: Cambridge Gdns thin house
places.description: This unusually narrow house in Cambridge Gardens exploits a constrained Notting Hill plot with a façade only a few metres wide. Its stacked rooms and compressed street presence demonstrate how London builders turned leftover urban land into habitable architecture.
places.descriptionIt: Questa casa insolitamente stretta di Cambridge Gardens sfrutta un lotto limitato di Notting Hill con una facciata larga pochi metri. Stanze sovrapposte e presenza compressa sulla strada mostrano come i costruttori londinesi trasformassero residui di terreno urbano in architettura abitabile.

places.name: Casa doppia facciata
places.description: This Spitalfields building presents two contrasting façades, making one structure read like neighbouring houses from different periods. The visual split reflects adaptation within a densely layered conservation area, where altered fronts often conceal connected interiors and older fabric.

La divisione visiva riflette gli adattamenti in un’area storica stratificata, dove fronti modificati nascondono spesso interni collegati e tessuti più antichi.

places.name: Castle Farm
places.description: Castle Farm near Shoreham in Kent is a working lavender farm rather than a London attraction. Summer fields, distillation and farm-shop products explain the agricultural source of lavender oil, but flowering, tickets and access are seasonal and the site lies well beyond Greater London.
places.descriptionIt: Castle Farm vicino a Shoreham, nel Kent, è una fattoria di lavanda attiva e non un’attrazione londinese. Campi estivi, distillazione e prodotti del negozio mostrano l’origine agricola dell’olio di lavanda, ma fioritura, biglietti e accesso sono stagionali e il sito è fuori dalla Greater London.

places.name: Charlie Chaplin Plaque
places.description: The plaque marks Charlie Chaplin’s South London beginnings, linking an ordinary streetscape to the childhood poverty and music-hall culture that shaped one of cinema’s defining performers. The building is private, so the value lies in the precise biographical marker.
places.descriptionIt: La targa ricorda le origini sud-londinesi di Charlie Chaplin, collegando una strada ordinaria alla povertà infantile e al music hall che formarono uno dei protagonisti fondamentali del cinema. L’edificio è privato: il valore sta nel preciso riferimento biografico.

places.name: Chequer Street Wooden Paving
places.description: A short patch of end-grain timber blocks survives beside Bunhill Fields, recalling wooden road surfaces once used to reduce wheel noise in Victorian London. The material proved slippery and difficult to maintain, which helps explain why such paving is now exceptionally rare.
places.descriptionIt: Un breve tratto di blocchi di legno disposti di testa sopravvive accanto a Bunhill Fields, ricordando le pavimentazioni usate per ridurre il rumore delle ruote nella Londra vittoriana. Il materiale era scivoloso e difficile da mantenere, motivo della sua attuale rarità.

places.name: Chinatown Gate
places.description: The ornamental gate on Wardour Street marks a principal entrance to London’s Chinatown. Completed in 2016 in a Qing-dynasty style by Chinese artisans, its tiled roof, painted brackets and guardian figures create a ceremonial threshold rather than merely a traffic marker.
places.descriptionIt: Il portale ornamentale di Wardour Street segna uno degli ingressi principali alla Chinatown londinese. Completato nel 2016 in stile Qing da artigiani cinesi, con tetto di tegole, mensole dipinte e figure guardiane, crea una soglia cerimoniale e non un semplice segnale stradale.

places.name: Christ Church Garden
places.description: Christ Church Garden occupies the former churchyard of Christ Church Greyfriars, whose Wren church was destroyed during the Blitz. Rose beds trace the footprint of the vanished nave and a small drinking fountain survives among the planting, turning bomb damage into a legible garden plan.

Aiuole di rose seguono l’impronta della navata scomparsa e una piccola fontanella sopravvive tra le piante, trasformando i danni di guerra in una pianta leggibile.

places.description: The cast-iron dragon on a pedestal marks the western boundary of the City of London. Derived from the dragon supporters of the City’s coat of arms, these sentinels appear at major road entrances and indicate the transition into the Square Mile’s separate civic jurisdiction.

places.name: Clattern Bridge
places.description: Clattern Bridge crosses the Hogsmill in Kingston and incorporates medieval stonework dating from around the twelfth century. Still carrying road traffic, its low arches survive beside the Coronation Stone, making an unusually compact encounter with infrastructure used continuously for centuries.

places.name: Cleopatra's Needle
places.description: Cleopatra’s Needle is an ancient Egyptian obelisk made for Pharaoh Thutmose III and brought to London in 1878. Victorian bronze sphinxes, bomb damage from the First World War and a time capsule buried beneath its base add later London layers to a monument far older than the city.

Sfingi bronzee vittoriane, danni della Prima guerra mondiale e una capsula del tempo sotto la base aggiungono strati londinesi a un monumento molto più antico della città.

Concrete bays 52–53 frame masonry from the city fortifications, creating the startling contrast of ancient defensive fabric surviving among ramps, painted lines and parked cars.

places.name: Coronation Stone
places.description: Kingston’s Coronation Stone is traditionally associated with the crowning of several Anglo-Saxon kings. The sarsen block now stands on a purpose-built base near the Guildhall, with metal lettering naming rulers whose ceremonies helped give Kingston its royal identity.
places.descriptionIt: La Coronation Stone di Kingston è tradizionalmente associata all’incoronazione di diversi re anglosassoni. Il blocco di sarsen si trova oggi su una base apposita vicino alla Guildhall, con lettere metalliche che nominano i sovrani le cui cerimonie diedero a Kingston la sua identità reale.

places.description: Fulham Football Club’s Craven Cottage is unusual for the red-brick pavilion and the surviving cottage tucked into a corner of the riverside stadium. Archibald Leitch’s listed stand and the intimate Thames setting preserve a scale largely lost at modern elite football grounds.

places.name: Crossness Pumping Station
places.description: Crossness Pumping Station opened in 1865 as the eastern end of Bazalgette’s sewer system. Its restored beam engines stand within exuberant cast-iron columns painted in Victorian colours, turning essential sanitation machinery into one of London’s most spectacular industrial interiors.

Le macchine a bilanciere restaurate si trovano tra esuberanti colonne in ghisa dipinte nei colori vittoriani, trasformando l’ingegneria sanitaria in uno degli interni industriali più spettacolari di Londra.

places.description: The Crystal Palace sphinxes were created in the 1850s for Joseph Paxton’s Egyptian Court after the exhibition building moved to Sydenham. They flank terraces that once introduced reconstructed ancient architecture, surviving as monumental fragments of a Victorian attempt to display world history.

places.description: The Crystal Palace Subway was built in 1865 as an ornate entrance linking the High Level railway station to the Crystal Palace. Fan-vaulted brickwork, patterned stone and Moorish-influenced details create a ceremonial underground space, now accessible through scheduled openings after restoration.

Volte a ventaglio in mattoni, pietra decorata e dettagli d’ispirazione moresca creano uno spazio sotterraneo cerimoniale, oggi accessibile con aperture programmate dopo il restauro.

places.name: Cutty Sark
places.description: Cutty Sark is an 1869 tea clipper preserved in dry dock at Greenwich. The ship’s copper-clad hull is suspended above a glazed visitor space, allowing the unusual experience of walking directly beneath a vessel built for speed on the China tea and Australian wool routes.
places.descriptionIt: Cutty Sark è un clipper del tè del 1869 conservato in bacino a Greenwich. Lo scafo rivestito in rame è sospeso sopra uno spazio vetrato, permettendo l’insolita esperienza di camminare direttamente sotto una nave costruita per la velocità sulle rotte del tè cinese e della lana australiana.

places.description: David Mach’s Out of Order consists of twelve red telephone boxes apparently toppling into one another in Kingston. Installed in 1989, the sculpture turns an increasingly obsolete piece of British street furniture into a frozen comic chain reaction.

places.description: Down Street Mews gives a surface clue to the disused Down Street Underground station below Piccadilly. Closed to passengers in 1932, the station later housed protected wartime railway operations and was used by Winston Churchill’s staff before the Cabinet War Rooms were ready.

places.name: Duck Island Cottage
places.description: Duck Island Cottage is a picturesque nineteenth-century lodge beside the lake in St James’s Park. Its rustic Tudor-Gothic appearance disguises a practical role connected with the park’s bird keeper and waterfowl, continuing the island’s long association with ducks and royal ornithology.

L’aspetto rustico Tudor-Gothic nasconde una funzione pratica legata al guardiano degli uccelli e agli anatidi, continuando la lunga associazione dell’isola con anatre e ornitologia reale.

places.name: Earls Court Police Box
places.description: The blue police box outside Earl’s Court station is a modern Metropolitan Police installation designed in the visual tradition of 1920s boxes. Its resemblance to Doctor Who’s TARDIS made it a pop-cultural landmark, although it was installed decades after the television prop’s original model.

places.name: Elfin Oak
places.description: The Elfin Oak is the hollow trunk of an ancient oak carved by Ivor Innes in 1928–30 with tiny fairies, gnomes, animals and witches. Protected beneath a canopy near the Diana Memorial Playground, it combines natural wood forms with a densely populated miniature fantasy world.

places.description: The green cabmen’s shelter at Embankment Place is one of the small roadside huts created from the 1870s to provide licensed cab drivers with hot food and rest without leaving their vehicles far away. Most survive as working facilities reserved for drivers.
places.descriptionIt: Il rifugio verde per tassisti di Embankment Place è una delle piccole strutture stradali create dagli anni Settanta dell’Ottocento per offrire ai conducenti autorizzati cibo caldo e riposo senza allontanarsi dai veicoli. La maggior parte resta una struttura operativa riservata ai tassisti.

places.name: Emirates Air Line - Canning Town Station
places.description: The cable-car terminal at Royal Victoria Dock carries gondolas across the Thames to the Greenwich Peninsula. Formerly branded Emirates Air Line and now the IFS Cloud Cable Car, it functions as public transport and an aerial viewpoint, with towers and haul ropes forming an unusual part of East London’s skyline.

Già Emirates Air Line e oggi IFS Cloud Cable Car, funziona come trasporto pubblico e punto panoramico aereo, con piloni e funi diventati parte insolita dello skyline della Londra est.

places.name: Fake no.10
places.description: The doorway at 10 Adam Street closely resembles the famous entrance to 10 Downing Street, making it a popular stand-in for photographs. Robert Adam’s eighteenth-century terrace is genuine, but this is an ordinary private address with different proportions and fittings, not a replica built as an attraction.

La terrazza settecentesca di Robert Adam è autentica, ma si tratta di un normale indirizzo privato con proporzioni e dettagli diversi, non di una replica turistica.

places.name: Former Victorian Pissoir
places.description: This cast-iron structure is a surviving Victorian street urinal, designed to provide discreet public sanitation within a compact metal screen. No longer serving its original purpose, it records an era when municipal engineering addressed bodily needs directly in the streetscape.

Non più usato per lo scopo originario, testimonia un’epoca in cui l’ingegneria municipale affrontava direttamente i bisogni corporei nello spazio urbano.

places.name: Former York Road tube station
places.description: York Road was a Piccadilly line station between King’s Cross and Caledonian Road, open from 1906 to 1932. Street-level remnants and the tiled station building mark platforms that still lie beside operational tracks, making it a visible fragment of London’s abandoned Underground network.
places.descriptionIt: York Road fu una stazione della Piccadilly line tra King’s Cross e Caledonian Road, aperta dal 1906 al 1932. Resti a livello stradale e l’edificio rivestito indicano banchine ancora accanto ai binari in uso, rendendola un frammento visibile della rete metropolitana abbandonata.

places.name: Freddie Mercury Memorial
places.description: A memorial near Heathrow commemorates Freddie Mercury, who was born Farrokh Bulsara in Zanzibar and spent part of his youth nearby after his family moved to Britain. The location connects his global stage identity with the quieter suburban geography of his early British life.
places.descriptionIt: Un memoriale vicino a Heathrow ricorda Freddie Mercury, nato Farrokh Bulsara a Zanzibar e vissuto da giovane nei dintorni dopo il trasferimento della famiglia in Gran Bretagna. Il luogo collega la sua identità scenica mondiale alla geografia suburbana dei primi anni britannici.

places.description: Gentle Monster’s Selfridges concession treats eyewear retail as installation art, using kinetic sculpture, oversized figures and surreal display machinery. The changing set is part shop and part temporary spectacle, so the precise objects may differ while the deliberately uncanny approach remains.

L’allestimento cambia ed è insieme negozio e spettacolo temporaneo: gli oggetti possono variare, ma resta l’approccio volutamente perturbante.

places.description: Gerry Dalton transformed his West London home and garden into a dense handmade world of concrete figures, classical ruins and personal mythology over several decades. places.description: God’s Own Junkyard fills a Walthamstow warehouse with neon signs, film props and light works made or collected by the Bracey family. The dense glow preserves fragments of Soho, fairgrounds and screen production, with a café-bar embedded inside the working collection.

places.description: The north entrance of Greenwich Foot Tunnel descends by lift and spiral stairs to a cast-iron-lined pedestrian passage beneath the Thames. Opened in 1902 for dock workers, the tunnel still connects the Isle of Dogs with Greenwich, with repaired sections revealing its long battle against leaks.

Aperto nel 1902 per i lavoratori dei docks, collega ancora Isle of Dogs e Greenwich; le sezioni riparate mostrano la lunga lotta contro le infiltrazioni.

places.name: Hammersmith Bridge
places.description: Hammersmith Bridge is Joseph Bazalgette’s ornate 1887 suspension bridge, decorated with heraldic metalwork and green-painted towers. Structural cracking closed it to motor traffic, making its restricted status part of a continuing engineering story rather than simply a picturesque Thames crossing.

Le crepe strutturali lo hanno chiuso al traffico automobilistico: le limitazioni sono parte di una storia ingegneristica ancora in corso, non solo di un pittoresco attraversamento del Tamigi.

places.description: Hankey Garden incorporates reused wartime stretchers into its railings, recognisable by their curved handholds. Like similar South London examples, the practical conversion turned surplus civil-defence equipment into permanent neighbourhood infrastructure after the Second World War.
places.descriptionIt: Hankey Garden incorpora nelle recinzioni barelle belliche riutilizzate, riconoscibili dalle impugnature curve. Come in altri esempi della Londra sud, la conversione trasformò attrezzature di difesa civile in infrastruttura permanente di quartiere dopo la Seconda guerra mondiale.

places.name: HMS Belfast
places.description: HMS Belfast is a Second World War-era light cruiser permanently moored on the Thames. Nine decks preserve gun turrets, engine spaces, mess rooms and cramped working areas, showing the ship as a complex floating community rather than only a dramatic silhouette beside Tower Bridge.

Nove ponti conservano torrette, motori, mense e spazi di lavoro angusti, mostrando la nave come una complessa comunità galleggiante e non solo una sagoma accanto a Tower Bridge.

places.description: Holborn Viaduct was opened in 1869 to carry a level road across the steep Fleet Valley. Its pavilions, statues and iron staircases disguise a major piece of Victorian traffic engineering, while streets and structures continue at the lower level beneath the bridge.

places.description: Horse Guards is the eighteenth-century ceremonial gateway between Whitehall and Horse Guards Parade. Mounted sentries and the clocked arch remain part of an active military site; the famous clock carries a dark mark traditionally linked, without firm proof, to the execution time of Charles I.

Sentinelle a cavallo e arco con orologio fanno parte di un sito militare attivo; sul quadrante compare un segno scuro tradizionalmente, ma senza prova certa, collegato all’esecuzione di Carlo I.

places.description: University College London displays philosopher Jeremy Bentham’s preserved ‘Auto-Icon’: his clothed skeleton seated in a cabinet, with a wax head replacing the unsuccessfully preserved original. The display embodies Bentham’s utilitarian wish to remain useful after death and is now housed in UCL’s student centre.

places.description: The present London Bridge is a restrained concrete crossing opened in 1973, replacing the nineteenth-century bridge sold and reconstructed in Arizona. Its apparent ordinariness masks a site where successive bridges have channelled London’s movement and commerce for nearly two millennia.

places.name: London Eye
places.description: The London Eye is a 135-metre observation wheel built for the millennium, with passenger capsules mounted outside the rim to preserve uninterrupted views. Its slow continuous rotation normally allows boarding without stopping, turning engineering mechanics into a thirty-minute moving panorama.
places.descriptionIt: Il London Eye è una ruota panoramica di 135 metri costruita per il millennio, con capsule montate all’esterno del cerchio per mantenere la vista libera. La lenta rotazione continua consente normalmente l’imbarco senza fermarsi, trasformando la meccanica in un panorama mobile di trenta minuti.

places.name: London Stone (remaining part)
places.description: The London Stone is a small block of limestone with a remarkably large mythology. Recorded for centuries on Cannon Street, it has been claimed as a Roman milestone, civic talisman and object of legend; the surviving fragment is displayed behind protective glass.
places.descriptionIt: La London Stone è un piccolo blocco di calcare circondato da una mitologia sorprendentemente vasta. Documentata per secoli in Cannon Street, è stata interpretata come pietra miliare romana, talismano civico e oggetto leggendario; il frammento superstite è esposto dietro un vetro protettivo.

places.name: London Wall
places.description: This exposed section of London’s defensive wall contains Roman masonry at its base and medieval rebuilding above. Standing beside later roads and towers, it makes the changing height, materials and repeated reuse of the city boundary legible at close range.
places.descriptionIt: Questo tratto esposto delle mura difensive di Londra contiene muratura romana alla base e ricostruzioni medievali sopra. Accanto a strade e torri successive, rende leggibili da vicino variazioni d’altezza, materiali e ripetuti riusi del confine cittadino.

places.name: Long doors
places.description: These exceptionally tall doors in Covent Garden exaggerate the proportions of an otherwise conventional façade. Their elongated panels likely respond to former commercial loading or theatrical use, creating a visual puzzle best understood by comparing them with the smaller surrounding openings.
places.descriptionIt: Queste porte eccezionalmente alte a Covent Garden esasperano le proporzioni di una facciata altrimenti normale. I pannelli allungati probabilmente rispondono a precedenti usi commerciali o teatrali, creando un enigma visivo da confrontare con le aperture più piccole circostanti.

places.name: Lower Robert st
places.description: Lower Robert Street is a dark service road beneath the raised Strand and Adelphi development. Concrete spans, ventilation noise and little daylight create an unusually cinematic undercroft, while rumours and ghost stories reflect how infrastructure hidden below prestigious streets acquires its own folklore.
places.descriptionIt: Lower Robert Street è una buia strada di servizio sotto lo Strand sopraelevato e lo sviluppo Adelphi. Campate in cemento, rumore della ventilazione e poca luce creano un sottosuolo cinematografico; voci e storie di fantasmi mostrano come l’infrastruttura nascosta sotto vie prestigiose generi un proprio folklore.

places.name: Merton Priory Chapter House
places.description: The chapter house foundations of medieval Merton Priory survive beneath the road and retail development near Colliers Wood. Interpretation reconstructs the scale of the Augustinian complex where Thomas Becket studied and where major medieval councils met, making archaeology visible in an unlikely modern setting.
places.descriptionIt: Le fondamenta della sala capitolare del medievale Merton Priory sopravvivono sotto la strada e lo sviluppo commerciale vicino a Colliers Wood. L’allestimento ricostruisce il complesso agostiniano dove studiò Thomas Becket e si tennero importanti concili, rendendo visibile l’archeologia in un ambiente moderno inatteso.

places.name: Michael Bond Grave
places.description: The grave of Paddington Bear creator Michael Bond stands in Paddington Old Cemetery. Its restrained headstone includes an affectionate reference to the courteous bear he gave the world, creating a quiet literary memorial rather than a themed attraction.
places.descriptionIt: La tomba di Michael Bond, creatore dell’orso Paddington, si trova nel Paddington Old Cemetery. La sobria lapide include un affettuoso richiamo all’educato orsetto donato al mondo, creando un tranquillo memoriale letterario e non un’attrazione tematica.

places.name: Millennium Maze
places.description: The Millennium Maze is a large pavement labyrinth in Northala Fields, set among the park’s conspicuous man-made hills. Its single winding route is designed for walking rather than getting lost, turning a traditional contemplative pattern into a piece of public landscape.
places.descriptionIt: Il Millennium Maze è un grande labirinto pavimentato a Northala Fields, tra le evidenti colline artificiali del parco. Il percorso unico e sinuoso è pensato per camminare, non per perdersi, trasformando un motivo contemplativo tradizionale in paesaggio pubblico.

places.name: Mimosa tree
places.description: A mature mimosa brings feathery foliage and bright winter blossom to this Pimlico streetscape. The tree is notable because its Mediterranean appearance contrasts with London’s climate and formal terraces; flowering varies with weather and should not be assumed year-round.
places.descriptionIt: Una mimosa adulta porta foglie leggere e vivace fioritura invernale in questa strada di Pimlico. L’albero è notevole perché l’aspetto mediterraneo contrasta con il clima londinese e le terrazze formali; la fioritura dipende dal meteo e non è presente tutto l’anno.

places.description: Mission: Breakout occupies part of the former South Kentish Town Underground station, closed to passengers in 1924. Escape-room games use the tiled passages and transport history of the disused station, providing rare commercial access to infrastructure otherwise hidden from the street.

places.name: Monument for a Dead Parrot
places.description: John Reardon’s 2009 painted-bronze cockatoo lies theatrically on its plinth in Greenwich. The absurd memorial is inevitably associated with Monty Python’s dead-parrot sketch, turning the solemn language of public monuments into a compact visual joke.
places.descriptionIt: Il cacatua in bronzo dipinto creato da John Reardon nel 2009 giace teatralmente sul piedistallo a Greenwich. L’assurdo memoriale richiama inevitabilmente lo sketch del pappagallo morto dei Monty Python, trasformando il linguaggio solenne dei monumenti pubblici in una battuta visiva.

places.description: The Monument to the Unknown Artist presents a life-size figure apparently drawing or measuring the riverside scene. By commemorating an unnamed creative worker rather than a famous individual, the sculpture playfully questions who receives public recognition.

Celebrando un lavoratore creativo senza nome invece di una personalità famosa, la scultura interroga con ironia chi riceve riconoscimento pubblico.

places.name: National Covid Memorial Wall
places.description: The National Covid Memorial Wall carries tens of thousands of hand-painted red hearts along the Thames opposite Parliament. Created by bereaved families and volunteers, each heart represents a life lost, making the wall both an evolving grassroots memorial and a public demand for remembrance.
places.descriptionIt: Il National Covid Memorial Wall porta decine di migliaia di cuori rossi dipinti a mano lungo il Tamigi di fronte al Parlamento. Creato da familiari e volontari, ogni cuore rappresenta una vita perduta, rendendo il muro insieme memoriale popolare in evoluzione e richiesta pubblica di memoria.

places.name: National Trust - Strand Lane "Roman Bath"
places.description: The so-called Roman Bath in Strand Lane is probably a seventeenth-century cistern associated with the former Arundel House water system, not an ancient Roman bathing pool. Later romantic promotion created the misleading name; the small chamber is viewed through a window or by arranged access.
places.descriptionIt: Il cosiddetto Roman Bath di Strand Lane è probabilmente una cisterna seicentesca legata al sistema idrico di Arundel House, non una vasca romana antica. La promozione romantica successiva generò il nome fuorviante; la piccola camera si osserva da una finestra o con accesso concordato.

places.name: Neals Yard
places.description: Neal’s Yard is a small Covent Garden courtyard whose brightly painted façades conceal cafés, wellness businesses and upper-level passages. Formerly a service yard, it was reshaped by alternative entrepreneur Nicholas Saunders and became a compact example of late twentieth-century urban reinvention.
places.descriptionIt: Neal’s Yard è un piccolo cortile di Covent Garden con facciate vivacemente dipinte che nascondono caffè, attività di benessere e passaggi ai piani superiori. Antico cortile di servizio, fu trasformato dall’imprenditore alternativo Nicholas Saunders in un esempio compatto di reinvenzione urbana tardo-novecentesca.

places.name: Necropolis station
places.description: The surviving façade at 121 Westminster Bridge Road belonged to the second London Necropolis station, opened in 1902. Special trains carried coffins and mourners to Brookwood Cemetery, separating classes and faiths in a unique railway system largely destroyed during the Blitz.
places.descriptionIt: La facciata superstite al 121 di Westminster Bridge Road apparteneva alla seconda stazione della London Necropolis Railway, aperta nel 1902. Treni speciali portavano bare e persone in lutto al Brookwood Cemetery, separando classi e confessioni in un sistema unico, in gran parte distrutto nel Blitz.

places.name: Nelson's Column
places.description: Nelson’s Column rises above Trafalgar Square with a statue of Admiral Nelson set on a Corinthian column. Four bronze lions, reliefs cast partly from captured cannon and the extreme height make familiar national symbolism depend on details that are difficult to inspect from ground level.
places.descriptionIt: Nelson’s Column domina Trafalgar Square con la statua dell’ammiraglio sopra una colonna corinzia. Quattro leoni di bronzo, rilievi fusi in parte da cannoni catturati e l’altezza estrema fanno dipendere il noto simbolismo nazionale da dettagli difficili da osservare dal basso.

places.description: The façades around New Inn Yard form a changing Shoreditch street-art canvas, with large commissions and smaller interventions wrapping brick walls above active studios and businesses. The work is temporary by nature, so changes are part of the site rather than damage to a fixed display.

Le opere sono temporanee per natura: i cambiamenti fanno parte del luogo e non sono danni a un’esposizione fissa.

places.name: Novelty Automation
places.description: Novelty Automation is artist Tim Hunkin’s arcade of hand-built satirical machines. Visitors operate coin-fed contraptions about bureaucracy, fame, money and everyday anxieties, reviving the seaside amusement arcade as mechanical theatre with an eccentric contemporary intelligence.
places.descriptionIt: Novelty Automation è la sala giochi di macchine satiriche costruite a mano dall’artista Tim Hunkin. I visitatori azionano con monete congegni su burocrazia, fama, denaro e ansie quotidiane, reinventando la sala giochi balneare come teatro meccanico dall’intelligenza contemporanea ed eccentrica.

places.name: Ouse Valley Viaduct
places.description: The Ouse Valley Viaduct carries the London–Brighton railway across the Sussex countryside on thirty-seven tall brick arches. Looking through the repeated piers creates a famously hypnotic perspective, but the structure lies outside London and must be approached using public paths without entering the railway.
places.descriptionIt: L’Ouse Valley Viaduct porta la ferrovia Londra–Brighton attraverso la campagna del Sussex su trentasette alti archi in mattoni. Guardare lungo i pilastri ripetuti crea una celebre prospettiva ipnotica, ma la struttura è fuori Londra e va raggiunta da sentieri pubblici senza entrare nella ferrovia.

places.name: Painted Hall
places.description: The Painted Hall at the Old Royal Naval College covers its walls and ceiling with Sir James Thornhill’s vast Baroque scheme celebrating monarchy, maritime power and the Protestant succession. Perspective tricks and allegorical figures earned it the nickname ‘Britain’s Sistine Chapel’.
places.descriptionIt: La Painted Hall dell’Old Royal Naval College copre pareti e soffitto con il vasto ciclo barocco di Sir James Thornhill, celebrazione di monarchia, potere marittimo e successione protestante. Prospettive illusionistiche e figure allegoriche le valsero il soprannome di “Cappella Sistina britannica”.

places.description: The golden figure of St Paul placed near the cathedral presents the apostle as a compact contemporary landmark against Wren’s much larger architecture. Its reflective surface and elevated position make the sculpture change dramatically with weather, light and viewing angle.

Superficie riflettente e posizione elevata fanno cambiare radicalmente la scultura con meteo, luce e angolo di osservazione.

places.description: Postman’s Park contains George Frederic Watts’s Memorial to Heroic Self-Sacrifice, a tiled loggia recording ordinary people who died saving others. The short, vivid inscriptions preserve Victorian and Edwardian tragedies without statues, making individual acts the monument’s central material.

Le brevi e vivide iscrizioni conservano tragedie vittoriane ed edoardiane senza statue, facendo dei singoli gesti il materiale centrale del monumento.

places.description: The Diana Memorial Fountain is a loop of Cornish granite through which water flows in contrasting smooth and turbulent channels. Visitors can approach and touch the water, making the memorial an inhabitable landscape rather than a conventional statue, though access changes in poor weather.
