places.description: This Earl’s Court flat was Diana Spencer’s home before her marriage to Prince Charles. The building is private, and its interest lies in the contrast between an ordinary shared London address and the intensely public royal life that followed.

places.description: Queen Caroline’s Bath is a surviving fragment of the demolished Montagu House in Greenwich Park. Despite the name, the sunken brick-and-stone structure may have served as a plunge pool or garden feature; its incomplete evidence makes the uncertainty part of the attraction.

places.name: Queen Elizabeth I Oak
places.description: The hollow veteran oak in Greenwich Park is traditionally associated with Queen Elizabeth I, though the precise royal stories are difficult to verify. Its immense decayed trunk is valuable as both living habitat and a focus for layers of park folklore.
places.descriptionIt: La grande quercia cava di Greenwich Park è tradizionalmente associata a Elisabetta I, anche se le storie reali precise sono difficili da verificare. L’enorme tronco in decomposizione ha valore sia come habitat vivente sia come centro di stratificazioni folkloriche del parco.

places.description: A small royal commemorative plaque is easy to miss at this mapped location. Its significance lies in the exact on-site inscription, which connects a specific ceremonial event or royal presence to otherwise everyday Kensington surroundings.

places.name: River Crane Brick (Shot) Tower
places.description: The River Crane shot tower is a tall brick remnant of the former gunpowder and metalworking landscape of west London. Molten lead was once dropped through towers to form spherical shot as it cooled; the surviving structure now stands among riverside greenery.
places.descriptionIt: La shot tower del River Crane è un alto residuo in mattoni dell’antico paesaggio di polverifici e lavorazione dei metalli della Londra ovest. Il piombo fuso veniva lasciato cadere nelle torri per formare pallini sferici raffreddandosi; la struttura oggi emerge tra il verde fluviale.

places.name: Robbie Williams House
places.description: This Holland Park property is associated with entertainer Robbie Williams, but it remains a private residence rather than a visitor site. Its mapped interest is celebrity geography only; observe the street architecture without photographing occupants or lingering at entrances.
places.descriptionIt: Questa proprietà di Holland Park è associata all’artista Robbie Williams, ma resta un’abitazione privata e non un luogo visitabile. L’interesse cartografico riguarda soltanto la geografia delle celebrità: osserva l’architettura della strada senza fotografare residenti o sostare agli ingressi.

places.name: Roman Fort Gate
places.description: The reconstructed west gate of London’s Roman fort is marked in the streets and structures near the Museum of London site. Foundations reveal how the military enclosure preceded and was later absorbed into the wider city wall.
places.descriptionIt: La porta occidentale ricostruita del forte romano di Londra è segnalata nelle strade e strutture vicino all’ex Museum of London. Le fondazioni mostrano come il recinto militare precedette e fu poi incorporato nelle mura cittadine più ampie.

places.name: Roman Wall
places.description: This Tower Hill section of wall preserves Roman stonework with medieval additions above. Nearby statues and interpretation make the construction phases visible, showing how London repeatedly repaired and reused the same defensive boundary.
places.descriptionIt: Questo tratto di mura a Tower Hill conserva muratura romana con aggiunte medievali sopra. Statue e pannelli vicini rendono visibili le fasi costruttive, mostrando come Londra abbia riparato e riutilizzato ripetutamente lo stesso confine difensivo.

places.name: Ruislip Lido Railway
places.description: Ruislip Lido Railway is a twelve-inch-gauge miniature railway running through woodland beside the reservoir and beach. Volunteer-operated trains connect two stations on selected days, making the journey itself a compact piece of working leisure engineering.
places.descriptionIt: Ruislip Lido Railway è una ferrovia in miniatura a scartamento di dodici pollici che attraversa il bosco accanto al bacino e alla spiaggia. Treni gestiti da volontari collegano due stazioni in giorni selezionati, trasformando il viaggio in un piccolo esempio di ingegneria ricreativa funzionante.

places.name: Russell Square Cabmen's Shelter
places.description: Russell Square’s green cabmen’s shelter is one of the surviving huts founded from the 1870s to provide licensed cab drivers with food and rest. It remains a working facility for drivers, so admire the compact timber design without treating it as a public café.
places.descriptionIt: Il rifugio verde per tassisti di Russell Square è una delle strutture superstiti create dagli anni Settanta dell’Ottocento per offrire cibo e riposo ai conducenti autorizzati. Resta un servizio operativo riservato: osserva il piccolo edificio in legno senza considerarlo un caffè pubblico.

places.description: The large aquarium inside Salesforce Tower brings a living aquatic display into a corporate office lobby. Visibility and access depend on building security and current tenant arrangements, so it should not be assumed to be an unrestricted public attraction.

places.name: Scoop House
places.description: Scoop House is a narrow contemporary house whose curved openings and carved-out forms respond to a constrained site near Bermondsey. Its sculptural façade is visible from the street, but the building is a private home rather than an architectural attraction with interior access.
places.descriptionIt: Scoop House è una stretta casa contemporanea le cui aperture curve e forme scavate rispondono a un lotto limitato vicino a Bermondsey. La facciata scultorea è visibile dalla strada, ma l’edificio è un’abitazione privata e non un’attrazione architettonica visitabile.

places.name: Sculpture by Pablo Reinoso
places.description: Pablo Reinoso’s public sculpture makes a familiar bench or structural element appear to escape into curling wooden lines. The work destabilises the boundary between functional street furniture and drawing in space, rewarding views from several angles.
places.descriptionIt: La scultura pubblica di Pablo Reinoso fa sembrare che una panchina o un elemento strutturale fugga in linee di legno ricurve. L’opera destabilizza il confine tra arredo funzionale e disegno nello spazio, e va osservata da più angolazioni.

places.name: Sewer Lamp
places.description: Carting Lane’s ornate lamp is associated with a Victorian system that drew sewer gas upward to be burned for street lighting and ventilation. The surviving post is often called London’s last sewer-gas lamp, though its mechanism and fuel were modified over time.
places.descriptionIt: L’elegante lampione di Carting Lane è legato a un sistema vittoriano che convogliava verso l’alto i gas fognari per bruciarli e illuminare ventilando. È spesso chiamato l’ultimo lampione a gas di fogna di Londra, anche se meccanismo e combustibile cambiarono nel tempo.

places.name: Shapes in the Clouds
places.description: Shapes in the Clouds is a playful public artwork that uses elevated forms to frame or echo the changing sky. Its appearance depends on viewpoint, daylight and weather, making the surrounding clouds an active part of the composition rather than a fixed background.
places.descriptionIt: Shapes in the Clouds è un’opera pubblica giocosa che usa forme elevate per incorniciare o riecheggiare il cielo mutevole. L’aspetto dipende da punto di vista, luce e meteo, rendendo le nuvole una parte attiva della composizione e non uno sfondo fisso.

places.name: Sharks!
places.description: Architect Jaimie Shorten’s Sharks! placed large shark sculptures in the Regent’s Canal as a deliberately absurd response to planning and public-space rules. The fins and bodies appear to invade the water beside Haggerston, turning bureaucratic friction into surreal public art.
places.descriptionIt: Sharks! dell’architetto Jaimie Shorten colloca grandi squali nel Regent’s Canal come risposta volutamente assurda alle regole urbanistiche e dello spazio pubblico. Pinne e corpi sembrano invadere l’acqua vicino a Haggerston, trasformando l’attrito burocratico in arte surreale.

places.name: Shepperton Lock
places.description: Shepperton Lock is a working Thames navigation lock where the old passenger ferry, riverside paths and boating life meet. The mapped ‘barcarolo’ interest is the small-scale river crossing and lock activity, both dependent on water conditions rather than fixed attraction hours.
places.descriptionIt: Shepperton Lock è una chiusa operativa del Tamigi dove si incontrano traghetto passeggeri, sentieri fluviali e vita nautica. L’interesse indicato come “barcarolo” riguarda la piccola traversata e l’attività della chiusa, entrambe dipendenti dalle condizioni dell’acqua più che da orari fissi.

places.name: Sherling Backstage Walkway
places.description: The Sherling Backstage Walkway at the National Theatre exposes scenery workshops and backstage circulation through a public route. It reveals theatre as manufacturing—sets, paint, props and logistics—rather than only the finished performance seen from an auditorium.
places.descriptionIt: La Sherling Backstage Walkway del National Theatre espone laboratori scenografici e percorsi dietro le quinte lungo un itinerario pubblico. Mostra il teatro come produzione—scene, pittura, oggetti e logistica—e non soltanto come spettacolo finito visto dalla platea.

places.name: Shirley Windmill
places.description: Shirley Windmill is a restored 1854 tower mill containing much of its original machinery. Volunteer open days explain grain lifting, grinding and wind control inside one of the few surviving large windmills in Greater London.
places.descriptionIt: Shirley Windmill è un mulino a torre restaurato del 1854 che conserva gran parte dei macchinari originali. Le giornate aperte gestite da volontari spiegano sollevamento del grano, macinazione e controllo del vento in uno dei pochi grandi mulini superstiti della Greater London.

places.name: Sir Winston Churchill Statue
places.description: Ivor Roberts-Jones’s bronze statue presents Winston Churchill standing heavily in Parliament Square, facing the Palace of Westminster. The simplified mass, walking stick and famously stern posture became the model for many later public images of the wartime prime minister.
places.descriptionIt: La statua bronzea di Ivor Roberts-Jones presenta Winston Churchill in posizione massiccia a Parliament Square, rivolto verso Westminster. La massa semplificata, il bastone e la celebre postura severa divennero modello per molte immagini pubbliche successive del primo ministro di guerra.

places.name: Soho Nose 1
places.description: One of Rick Buckley’s small plaster noses projects anonymously from a Soho façade. Installed in 1997 as a protest against surveillance cameras, the noses acquired elaborate false legends; their almost invisible scale is central to the joke.
places.descriptionIt: Uno dei piccoli nasi in gesso di Rick Buckley sporge anonimamente da una facciata di Soho. Installati nel 1997 come protesta contro le telecamere, i nasi generarono elaborate leggende false; la scala quasi invisibile è parte essenziale della battuta.

places.description: A discreet plaster nose by Rick Buckley hides on this Soho building, one of several installed without permission in 1997. The work’s anonymity encouraged myths about spies, artists and the Seven Noses of Soho.

places.description: A final mapped example of Rick Buckley’s Soho noses appears on this Covent Garden façade. The modest projection demonstrates how the project spread through central London and became folklore before its maker publicly explained it.

places.name: Spitalfields Charnel House
places.description: The glass-covered remains beside Spitalfields Market are a medieval charnel house built to store bones cleared from the cemetery of St Mary Spital. Its subterranean arches survive beneath the modern square, making death and redevelopment visibly overlap.
places.descriptionIt: I resti protetti dal vetro accanto a Spitalfields Market appartengono a un ossario medievale costruito per conservare le ossa rimosse dal cimitero di St Mary Spital. Gli archi sotterranei sopravvivono sotto la piazza moderna, sovrapponendo visibilmente morte e riqualificazione.

places.name: St Martin-in-the-Fields Church
places.description: St Martin-in-the-Fields is James Gibbs’s influential eighteenth-century church, whose classical portico and steeple were widely copied. Its crypt now contains a café and brass-rubbing centre, while concerts and social programmes keep the building active beyond worship.
places.descriptionIt: St Martin-in-the-Fields è l’influente chiesa settecentesca di James Gibbs, con portico classico e campanile ampiamente imitati. La cripta ospita oggi caffè e brass rubbing, mentre concerti e programmi sociali mantengono l’edificio attivo oltre il culto.

places.name: St Vedast/Foster - Blue door courtyard
places.description: A vivid blue door beside St Vedast-alias-Foster leads into a small courtyard hidden among City streets. The colour and compressed passage create a theatrical threshold to the Wren church’s quieter rear spaces.
places.descriptionIt: Una vivace porta blu accanto a St Vedast-alias-Foster conduce a un piccolo cortile nascosto tra le strade della City. Il colore e il passaggio compresso creano una soglia teatrale verso gli spazi più tranquilli dietro la chiesa di Wren.

places.name: Stronsa Road
places.description: Stronsa Road contains an unusually abrupt piece of west-London streetscape shaped by railway, industrial and residential boundaries. Its odd geometry is best understood on foot, where blank walls and constrained plots reveal how infrastructure divided the neighbourhood.
places.descriptionIt: Stronsa Road contiene un tratto insolitamente brusco di paesaggio urbano occidentale, modellato da confini ferroviari, industriali e residenziali. La geometria si comprende a piedi, dove muri ciechi e lotti stretti mostrano come l’infrastruttura abbia diviso il quartiere.

places.name: Tesco Kids Banksy no more
places.description: Banksy’s Tesco Kids mural once appeared on this Essex Road wall, satirising consumer branding and childhood ritual. The original work is no longer present, so the location documents London street art’s impermanence rather than offering a surviving Banksy.
places.descriptionIt: Il murale Tesco Kids di Banksy appariva un tempo su questo muro di Essex Road, satira del branding commerciale e dei rituali infantili. L’opera originale non è più presente: il luogo documenta l’impermanenza della street art londinese invece di offrire un Banksy superstite.

places.name: The Artist's Garden
places.description: The Artist’s Garden is a rooftop public-art space above Temple Underground station. Commissioned installations use planting, sculpture and the open skyline, turning transport infrastructure into a changing exhibition rather than a permanent conventional garden.
places.descriptionIt: The Artist’s Garden è uno spazio d’arte pubblica sul tetto della stazione Temple. Installazioni commissionate usano piante, sculture e cielo aperto, trasformando l’infrastruttura di trasporto in una mostra mutevole invece di un giardino convenzionale permanente.

places.name: The Blue Door Notting Hill Film
places.description: The blue door associated with the film Notting Hill marks the exterior used for William Thacker’s fictional home. The original prop colour and ownership have changed over time; it is a private residence, not a film museum.

places.name: The Castle Climbing Centre
places.description: The Castle Climbing Centre occupies a castellated Victorian water-pumping station in Stoke Newington. Turrets and thick brick walls now contain climbing routes, while former filter beds support gardens and outdoor activities.
places.descriptionIt: The Castle Climbing Centre occupa una stazione vittoriana di pompaggio dell’acqua dall’aspetto fortificato a Stoke Newington. Torrette e spessi muri in mattoni contengono oggi percorsi d’arrampicata, mentre gli antichi letti filtranti ospitano giardini e attività esterne.

places.name: The Cenotaph
places.description: The Cenotaph is Edwin Lutyens’s deliberately austere memorial to the dead of the First World War and later conflicts. Its apparently simple geometry subtly curves and tapers, creating a symbolic empty tomb rather than a literal military sculpture.
places.descriptionIt: The Cenotaph è il memoriale volutamente austero di Edwin Lutyens ai caduti della Prima guerra mondiale e dei conflitti successivi. La geometria apparentemente semplice curva e si assottiglia con discrezione, creando una tomba simbolica vuota invece di una scultura militare letterale.

places.name: The Golden Hinde
places.description: The Golden Hinde is a full-size reconstruction of the ship in which Francis Drake circumnavigated the globe. Moored in a confined Southwark dock, its compact decks reveal the cramped scale of sixteenth-century ocean travel, though the vessel itself dates from the twentieth century.
places.descriptionIt: The Golden Hinde è una ricostruzione a grandezza naturale della nave con cui Francis Drake circumnavigò il globo. Ormeggiata in un piccolo bacino di Southwark, mostra la scala angusta dei viaggi oceanici cinquecenteschi, anche se la nave attuale è del Novecento.

places.name: The Graffiti Tunnel
places.description: Leake Street Arches became a legal graffiti space after Banksy’s 2008 Cans Festival. Layers are constantly painted over, so the tunnel is a live working surface where change, fumes and active artists are part of the experience.
places.descriptionIt: Leake Street Arches divenne spazio legale per graffiti dopo il Cans Festival di Banksy del 2008. Gli strati vengono continuamente coperti: il tunnel è una superficie attiva dove cambiamento, odori di vernice e artisti al lavoro fanno parte dell’esperienza.

places.name: The Hardy Tree
places.description: The Hardy Tree grew among gravestones moved during the expansion of St Pancras railway, traditionally associated with the young Thomas Hardy’s work for an architect. The original ash collapsed after decay, but the site and stones preserve the powerful image and its railway-era story.
places.descriptionIt: The Hardy Tree crebbe tra lapidi spostate durante l’ampliamento della ferrovia di St Pancras, tradizionalmente legate al lavoro del giovane Thomas Hardy per un architetto. Il frassino originale è crollato dopo il degrado, ma luogo e pietre conservano l’immagine e la storia ferroviaria.

places.name: The Hill Garden and Pergola
places.description: The Hill Garden and Pergola is an elevated Edwardian walkway built for Lord Leverhulme above Hampstead Heath. Brick terraces, classical columns and climbing plants create long framed views, with weathering adding a romantic sense of partial ruin.

places.name: The House Mill
places.description: The House Mill at Three Mills is a major surviving tidal mill, rebuilt in 1776 on a much older milling site. Water wheels once drove machinery for flour and alcohol production; guided visits reveal the timber mechanisms and industrial landscape of the lower Lea.
places.descriptionIt: The House Mill a Three Mills è un grande mulino a marea superstite, ricostruito nel 1776 su un sito molto più antico. Le ruote idrauliche azionavano macchinari per farina e alcol; le visite guidate mostrano meccanismi in legno e paesaggio industriale del basso Lea.

places.name: The Iconic postbox
places.description: This distinctive postbox is valued for an unusual royal cipher, design detail or survival within the local streetscape. Inspect the casting and collection plate closely: small differences identify the reign and period more reliably than colour alone.

places.name: The Mosaic House Chiswick
places.description: Artist Carrie Reichardt has covered her Chiswick home with mosaics, ceramics, slogans and portraits created with collaborators. The façade turns a private suburban house into a dense public artwork addressing activism, community and social justice; view it respectfully from the pavement.

La facciata trasforma un’abitazione suburbana privata in una fitta opera pubblica su attivismo, comunità e giustizia sociale; va osservata con rispetto dal marciapiede.

places.name: The Nursemaids' Tunnel
places.description: The Nursemaids’ Tunnel is a pedestrian passage beneath Marylebone Road linking parts of the former estate landscape around Regent’s Park. Its name recalls the carers and children who used such segregated routes to cross busy roads away from carriage traffic.

places.name: The Old Curiosity Shop
places.description: The timber-framed building known as The Old Curiosity Shop dates largely from the sixteenth or seventeenth century and survived nearby redevelopment. Its Dickens association was applied after the novel rather than firmly proven, but the tiny shop remains a rare fragment of pre-Fire London.
places.descriptionIt: L’edificio a graticcio noto come The Old Curiosity Shop risale in gran parte al XVI o XVII secolo ed è sopravvissuto alla riqualificazione circostante. Il legame con Dickens fu attribuito dopo il romanzo e non è provato, ma il piccolo negozio resta un raro frammento della Londra precedente al Grande Incendio.

places.name: The Rolling Bridge
places.description: Thomas Heatherwick’s Rolling Bridge curls its eight steel-and-timber sections into a wheel to open the head of Paddington Basin. It is a kinetic sculpture that also functions as a footbridge, but demonstrations occur only at scheduled times.
places.descriptionIt: Il Rolling Bridge di Thomas Heatherwick arrotola otto sezioni in acciaio e legno formando una ruota per aprire il bacino di Paddington. È una scultura cinetica che funziona anche da passerella, ma le dimostrazioni avvengono solo in orari programmati.

places.name: The Thames Barrier
places.description: The Thames Barrier uses ten movable steel gates to protect London from tidal surges. When raised, the silver piers and rotating gates reveal flood defence as monumental river engineering; the riverside information centre explains forecasts and closures.

places.name: The Tide
places.description: The Tide is an elevated landscaped walkway winding through Greenwich Peninsula. Ramps, bridges and planting create changing Thames views while public artworks punctuate the route, combining park, promenade and infrastructure above the surrounding streets.
places.descriptionIt: The Tide è una passeggiata paesaggistica sopraelevata che attraversa Greenwich Peninsula. Rampe, ponti e piante creano vedute mutevoli sul Tamigi, intervallate da opere pubbliche, unendo parco, promenade e infrastruttura sopra le strade circostanti.

places.name: The Tin Tabernacle
places.description: Kilburn’s Tin Tabernacle is a corrugated-iron church erected in 1863 and later converted into the Sea Cadets’ HMS Bicester. Behind the fragile metal exterior, a mock ship interior and nautical fittings create an extraordinary collision of chapel and training vessel.
places.descriptionIt: Il Tin Tabernacle di Kilburn è una chiesa in lamiera ondulata eretta nel 1863 e poi trasformata nella sede dei Sea Cadets HMS Bicester. Dietro il fragile esterno metallico, interni da nave e arredi nautici creano uno straordinario incontro tra cappella e unità d’addestramento.

places.name: The Tower House - Casa di Jimmy Page
places.description: The Tower House is William Burges’s richly detailed Gothic Revival home, later owned by musician Jimmy Page. Its exterior turrets, carved stone and patterned brick hint at extraordinary interiors, but it remains a closely protected private residence.

places.description: The Notting Hill film’s fictional Travel Bookshop was inspired by a real specialist shop nearby, while this Portobello location supplied the screen exterior. The business shown in the film was a set, so today’s premises should be read as a location rather than the original fictional shop.

places.name: Thin House
places.description: This South Kensington ‘thin house’ uses a triangular plot created by converging streets. The end façade is only a few feet deep, while the building widens behind it, producing a convincing architectural illusion when seen head-on.

places.name: Three Bridges
places.description: Brunel’s Three Bridges at Hanwell stacks road, canal and railway at one junction: Windmill Lane above the Grand Union Canal, which crosses the railway in an iron trough. The compact composition solved three competing routes without an ordinary level crossing.

places.description: Tiny Wee Gallery compresses an independent art display into a window-sized space on a Spitalfields street. Changing work is viewed from the pavement rather than through a conventional staffed interior, making scale and accidental discovery central to the project.

places.name: Traffic Light Tree
places.description: Pierre Vivant’s Traffic Light Tree combines seventy-five sets of traffic lights into a branching public sculpture near Canary Wharf. Computer-controlled sequences replace practical road instructions with restless colour, turning familiar signals into an urban tree.

places.name: Trinity Buoy Lighthouse
places.description: Trinity Buoy Wharf’s Experimental Lighthouse was built in the 1860s for testing maritime lights and later associated with Michael Faraday’s optical work. It was never a normal navigational lighthouse; today the tower sits within a creative riverside complex and hosts Longplayer.
places.descriptionIt: L’Experimental Lighthouse di Trinity Buoy Wharf fu costruito negli anni Sessanta dell’Ottocento per provare luci marittime e fu poi associato agli studi ottici di Michael Faraday. Non fu mai un normale faro di navigazione; oggi sorge in un complesso creativo sul fiume e ospita Longplayer.

places.name: Twickenham Stadium
places.description: Twickenham Stadium is the home of English rugby union and the world’s largest dedicated rugby stadium. Tours reveal changing rooms, tunnel, royal box and museum, while the vast bowl dramatically transforms this otherwise suburban part of west London on match days.
places.descriptionIt: Twickenham Stadium è la casa del rugby union inglese e il più grande stadio al mondo dedicato a questo sport. Le visite mostrano spogliatoi, tunnel, royal box e museo, mentre l’enorme struttura trasforma radicalmente questa zona suburbana della Londra ovest nei giorni di partita.

places.name: Ugo Foscolo's first grave
places.description: Italian poet Ugo Foscolo was first buried at St Nicholas’s churchyard in Chiswick after dying in exile in 1827. His remains were later transferred to Santa Croce in Florence, leaving the original grave as a marker of displacement, memory and Anglo-Italian literary history.
places.descriptionIt: Il poeta italiano Ugo Foscolo fu sepolto inizialmente nel cimitero di St Nicholas a Chiswick dopo la morte in esilio nel 1827. Le spoglie furono poi trasferite a Santa Croce a Firenze, lasciando la prima tomba come segno di esilio, memoria e storia letteraria anglo-italiana.

places.name: University Boat Race Finishing Stone
places.description: The stone on the Thames path marks the finish line of the annual Oxford–Cambridge Boat Race. Its modest size contrasts with the event’s scale, fixing an invisible line across the river where closely fought races are decided.

places.name: Up at The O2
places.description: Up at The O2 is a guided climb over the fabric roof of the former Millennium Dome. Visitors wear harnesses and follow a suspended walkway to a central platform, experiencing the building’s cable-supported structure as terrain rather than seeing it only from below.

places.name: Upminster Windmill
places.description: Upminster Windmill is a smock mill built in 1803 and restored with working machinery, sails and cap. Volunteer open days explain how wind power drove several floors of milling equipment at what was once the rural edge of Essex.
places.descriptionIt: Upminster Windmill è un mulino a torre lignea costruito nel 1803 e restaurato con macchinari, pale e copertura funzionanti. Le aperture dei volontari spiegano come il vento azionasse più piani di attrezzature in quella che era la campagna dell’Essex.

places.name: V2 Rocket Memorial
places.description: The V2 memorial marks the Chiswick site where a German V2 rocket exploded in September 1944, the first to strike Britain. Its understated plaque anchors the beginning of a new and terrifying form of ballistic warfare to an ordinary residential street.

places.description: Victoria Park’s Chinese Pagoda is a modern reconstruction of the pavilion first created for the park in the 1840s. Standing on an island reached by an ornamental bridge, it restores an exotic focal point to the lake while clearly dating from a later rebuilding.
places.descriptionIt: La Chinese Pagoda di Victoria Park è una ricostruzione moderna del padiglione creato per il parco negli anni Quaranta dell’Ottocento. Su un’isola raggiunta da un ponte ornamentale, restituisce al lago un punto focale esotico pur appartenendo chiaramente a una ricostruzione successiva.

places.description: The weather vane of St Lawrence Jewry can be seen above the City roofline, its gilded form identifying Wren’s church beside Guildhall. The mapped viewpoint rewards looking upward from the correct street angle rather than entering a separate attraction.

places.description: Garden Lodge was Freddie Mercury’s Kensington home and remains a private residence. Fans historically left messages on its boundary wall, but the site has no public interior; respectful viewing should avoid obstructing neighbours or treating the entrance as a shrine.

places.name: Wigmore Hall
places.description: Wigmore Hall is an exceptionally intimate 1901 concert hall known for chamber music and song. Its Arts and Crafts interior culminates in a cupola mural above the stage, while famously clear acoustics make subtle performances unusually immediate.
places.descriptionIt: Wigmore Hall è una sala da concerto del 1901 eccezionalmente intima, celebre per musica da camera e canto. L’interno Arts and Crafts culmina in un dipinto nella cupola sopra il palco, mentre l’acustica limpida rende le esecuzioni più sottili insolitamente immediate.

places.name: William Willett Memorial and Sundial
places.description: The memorial and sundial honour William Willett, the Petts Wood campaigner whose advocacy helped introduce daylight saving time in Britain. The sun-based instrument is an apt tribute to a man who wanted society’s clocks to make better use of summer light.
places.descriptionIt: Il memoriale e la meridiana ricordano William Willett, promotore di Petts Wood la cui campagna contribuì all’introduzione dell’ora legale in Gran Bretagna. Lo strumento solare è un omaggio appropriato a chi voleva che gli orologi sociali sfruttassero meglio la luce estiva.

places.description: Wilton’s Music Hall preserves a mid-nineteenth-century auditorium behind a row of older East End houses and pub rooms. Layers of peeling paint, galleries and later repairs reveal survival rather than polished reconstruction, while performances continue the building’s original purpose.
places.descriptionIt: Wilton’s Music Hall conserva un auditorium ottocentesco dietro una fila di case e locali più antichi dell’East End. Strati di pittura, gallerie e riparazioni successive mostrano sopravvivenza più che ricostruzione patinata, mentre gli spettacoli continuano la funzione originaria.

places.description: 1st Place at Chumleigh Gardens is an early-years nursery set within Burgess Park, not a freely accessible public garden attraction. Its outdoor spaces use the multicultural gardens and park setting for play and learning, but entry is for enrolled families, staff and arranged visitors.

places.name: All Hallows' Churchyard
places.description: All Hallows’ Churchyard, also called Copperfield Street Community Garden, occupies the walled site of George Gilbert Scott Jr’s church, destroyed during the Second World War. Local volunteers have tended its lawn, flower beds, shrubs and surviving fabric for decades as a secluded Southwark garden.

Da decenni volontari locali curano prato, aiuole, arbusti e resti architettonici come raccolto giardino di Southwark.

places.name: Barnsbury Wood Nature Reserve
places.description: Barnsbury Wood is Islington’s smallest local nature reserve and its only surviving mature woodland. The site grew from the garden of a nineteenth-century house; ash, sycamore, lime and horse chestnut now shelter deadwood insects, birds and shade plants along a short path opened only at limited times.
places.descriptionIt: Barnsbury Wood è la più piccola riserva naturale locale di Islington e il suo unico bosco maturo superstite. Nata dal giardino di una casa ottocentesca, ospita frassini, sicomori, tigli e ippocastani che proteggono insetti del legno morto, uccelli e piante d’ombra lungo un breve sentiero aperto solo in orari limitati.

places.name: Battersea Park
places.description: Battersea Park was laid out beside the Thames in the 1850s on former market gardens and marsh. Its carriage drives, boating lake, sub-tropical garden, riverside promenade, Peace Pagoda, sports grounds and surviving Festival of Britain features create an unusually varied Victorian municipal park.
places.descriptionIt: Battersea Park fu progettato lungo il Tamigi negli anni 1850 su antichi orti e paludi. Viali, lago navigabile, giardino subtropicale, passeggiata fluviale, Peace Pagoda, campi sportivi e resti del Festival of Britain compongono un parco municipale vittoriano insolitamente vario.

places.name: Beckenham Place Park
places.description: Beckenham Place Park is Lewisham’s largest green space, centred on an eighteenth-century Palladian mansion built for John Cator. Ancient woodland, grassland, historic park trees and the River Ravensbourne surround a restored lake for swimming and paddling, community gardens and extensive walking routes.
places.descriptionIt: Beckenham Place Park è il più grande spazio verde di Lewisham, centrato su una villa palladiana settecentesca costruita per John Cator. Bosco antico, prati, alberi storici e il fiume Ravensbourne circondano un lago restaurato per nuoto e pagaia, giardini comunitari e numerosi sentieri.

places.name: Bernie Spain Gardens
places.description: Bernie Spain Gardens form two riverside lawns at the centre of the Coin Street neighbourhood, between Gabriel’s Wharf and Oxo Tower Wharf. Named for a local housing campaigner, the space hosts festivals and community events while its lawns, borders and views open a public pause on the South Bank.
places.descriptionIt: Bernie Spain Gardens comprende due prati lungo il fiume nel cuore del quartiere Coin Street, tra Gabriel’s Wharf e Oxo Tower Wharf. Intitolato a un’attivista per l’edilizia popolare, ospita festival ed eventi comunitari; prati, bordure e vedute offrono uno spazio pubblico sulla South Bank.

places.name: Bonnington Square Pleasure Garden
places.description: Bonnington Square Pleasure Garden was created by residents who reclaimed a Second World War bomb site beside their Vauxhall housing co-operative. Dense subtropical planting, a communal wheel sculpture, paths and informal seating give the tiny garden the inventive, self-managed character of Bonnington Square.
places.descriptionIt: Bonnington Square Pleasure Garden fu creato dagli abitanti che recuperarono un sito bombardato durante la Seconda guerra mondiale accanto alla loro cooperativa residenziale di Vauxhall. Fitta vegetazione subtropicale, una scultura a ruota, sentieri e sedute informali esprimono il carattere creativo e autogestito di Bonnington Square.

places.name: Brent Lodge Park
places.description: Brent Lodge Park follows the River Brent through the former grounds of Brent Lodge in Hanwell. Known locally as the Bunny Park, it combines riverside meadows, veteran trees, playgrounds and sports with a free animal centre, maze and the adjoining Millennium woodland.
places.descriptionIt: Brent Lodge Park segue il fiume Brent negli antichi terreni di Brent Lodge a Hanwell. Conosciuto localmente come Bunny Park, unisce prati fluviali, alberi veterani, giochi e sport a un centro animali gratuito, un labirinto e il vicino bosco del Millennium.

places.name: Brockwell Park
places.description: Brockwell Park climbs from Herne Hill to broad skyline views around Brockwell Hall. Opened to the public in 1892, it contains walled and community gardens, ponds, mature avenues, sports grounds, a miniature railway and the Grade II-listed 1930s lido.
places.descriptionIt: Brockwell Park sale da Herne Hill verso ampie vedute dello skyline attorno a Brockwell Hall. Aperto al pubblico nel 1892, comprende giardino murato e comunitario, stagni, viali maturi, campi sportivi, ferrovia in miniatura e il lido degli anni Trenta classificato Grade II.

places.name: Brooks Farm
places.description: Brooks Farm is a community teaching farm in Leyton’s Jack Cornwell Park. Cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, ponies, donkeys and small animals support school visits and family learning, while the surrounding park provides play and recreation for a densely built part of Waltham Forest.
places.descriptionIt: Brooks Farm è una fattoria didattica comunitaria nel Jack Cornwell Park di Leyton. Bovini, pecore, capre, maiali, pony, asini e piccoli animali sostengono visite scolastiche e apprendimento familiare; il parco circostante offre gioco e svago in una zona densamente costruita di Waltham Forest.

places.name: Bushy Park
places.description: Bushy Park is the second largest Royal Park, shaped by Tudor hunting, seventeenth-century water engineering and centuries of grazing. Chestnut Avenue leads to Sir Christopher Wren’s Diana Fountain, while deer herds, acid grassland, ponds, woodland gardens and the restored Water Gardens spread around Hampton Court’s northern approach.
places.descriptionIt: Bushy Park è il secondo Royal Park per estensione, modellato dalla caccia Tudor, dall’ingegneria idraulica seicentesca e da secoli di pascolo. Chestnut Avenue conduce alla Diana Fountain di Christopher Wren; mandrie di cervi, praterie acide, stagni, giardini boscosi e Water Gardens restaurati circondano l’accesso nord a Hampton Court.

places.name: Camley Street Natural Park
places.description: Camley Street Natural Park is a former coal yard transformed by the London Wildlife Trust into a nature reserve beside the Regent’s Canal. Reedbeds, ponds, woodland and meadow support wetland wildlife within King’s Cross, while boardwalks, a learning centre and floating habitat bring visitors close to an urban ecosystem.
places.descriptionIt: Camley Street Natural Park è un ex deposito di carbone trasformato dal London Wildlife Trust in riserva naturale lungo il Regent’s Canal. Canneti, stagni, bosco e prato sostengono la fauna nel cuore di King’s Cross; passerelle, centro didattico e habitat galleggianti avvicinano i visitatori a un ecosistema urbano.

places.name: Cannizaro Park
places.description: Cannizaro Park was once the private garden of the adjoining country house and became a public park in 1949. Its carefully managed collection includes an Italian garden, rose garden, Mediterranean beds, water garden, rare trees and woodland, all unfolding in distinct garden rooms beside Wimbledon Common.
places.descriptionIt: Cannizaro Park fu il giardino privato della villa adiacente e divenne parco pubblico nel 1949. La collezione accuratamente curata comprende giardino italiano, roseto, aiuole mediterranee, giardino d’acqua, alberi rari e bosco, distribuiti in stanze verdi accanto a Wimbledon Common.

places.description: This small gated garden sits over a medieval plague burial ground and beside the Charterhouse, surrounded by plane trees, medical institutions and layered monastic and residential history.

places.name: Chiswick House and Gardens
places.description: Chiswick House Gardens surround Lord Burlington’s neo-Palladian villa with one of the most influential early English landscape gardens. William Kent’s vistas, statues, lake, cascade and classical buildings survive alongside formal gardens, a conservatory with historic camellias and later public-park planting.
places.descriptionIt: I giardini di Chiswick House circondano la villa neopalladiana di Lord Burlington con uno dei primi e più influenti paesaggi all’inglese. Prospettive, statue, lago, cascata ed edifici classici di William Kent convivono con giardini formali, una serra di camelie storiche e sistemazioni successive da parco pubblico.

places.name: Clissold Park
places.description: Clissold Park occupies the grounds of eighteenth-century Clissold House beside the medieval parish church of St Mary. Its lakes began as New River reservoirs; today deer and animal enclosures, an aviary, playgrounds, sports fields, mature avenues and the restored house make it Stoke Newington’s principal civic park.
places.descriptionIt: Clissold Park occupa i terreni della settecentesca Clissold House accanto alla chiesa medievale di St Mary. I laghi nacquero come serbatoi del New River; oggi recinti con daini e animali, voliera, giochi, campi sportivi, viali maturi e la casa restaurata ne fanno il principale parco civico di Stoke Newington.

places.name: Coombe Wood Gardens
places.description: Coombe Wood Gardens occupy part of the former Coombe Wood House estate on the wooded slopes above Croydon. Formal terraces, ponds, a rock garden, ornamental shrubs and a broad lawn lead into woodland renowned for spring rhododendrons, azaleas and bluebells.
places.descriptionIt: Coombe Wood Gardens occupa parte dell’antica tenuta di Coombe Wood House sui pendii boscosi sopra Croydon. Terrazze formali, stagni, roccaglia, arbusti ornamentali e un grande prato conducono nel bosco, celebre in primavera per rododendri, azalee e campanule.

places.name: Crossbones Garden
places.description: Crossbones Garden is a memorial on the edge of the medieval burial ground used for poor and marginalised people, including women known as the Winchester Geese. Ribbons and personal dedications cover its gates, while community planting, sculpture and ceremonies honour people historically excluded from consecrated ground.
places.descriptionIt: Crossbones Garden è un memoriale ai margini del cimitero medievale destinato a poveri ed emarginati, comprese le donne note come Winchester Geese. Nastri e dediche personali coprono i cancelli; piante comunitarie, sculture e cerimonie ricordano chi fu storicamente escluso dal terreno consacrato.

places.hook: Ribbons, planting and ritual honour the outcast dead of Southwark’s medieval Cross Bones burial ground.
places.hookIt: Nastri, piante e rituali onorano i morti emarginati dell’antico cimitero Cross Bones di Southwark.

places.name: Crystal Palace Dinosaurs
places.description: The Crystal Palace Dinosaurs are more than thirty life-size sculptures created by Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins in the 1850s around lakes in Crystal Palace Park. Based on the earliest scientific reconstructions of extinct animals, their now-outdated anatomy records a pivotal moment when prehistoric life first entered public imagination.
places.descriptionIt: I Crystal Palace Dinosaurs sono oltre trenta sculture a grandezza naturale create da Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins negli anni 1850 attorno ai laghi di Crystal Palace Park. Basate sulle prime ricostruzioni scientifiche di animali estinti, le anatomie oggi superate documentano il momento in cui la preistoria entrò nell’immaginario pubblico.

places.name: Crystal Palace Park Farm
places.description: Crystal Palace Park Farm is a small educational farm within the park, operated by Capel Manor College. Visitors can encounter farm animals and learn about husbandry, while students train in animal care beside the Victorian park’s lakes, terraces and celebrated dinosaur sculptures.
places.descriptionIt: Crystal Palace Park Farm è una piccola fattoria didattica nel parco, gestita da Capel Manor College. I visitatori incontrano animali da fattoria e scoprono il loro allevamento, mentre gli studenti si formano nella cura animale accanto ai laghi, alle terrazze e ai celebri dinosauri vittoriani del parco.

places.hookIt: Una fattoria didattica porta formazione nella cura degli animali e incontri ravvicinati con il bestiame dentro Crystal Palace Park.

places.name: Culpeper Community Garden
places.description: Culpeper Community Garden has occupied former housing land near the Angel since 1982. Shared lawns and ponds sit beside individual organic plots, wildlife planting and a children’s area, while volunteers, schools and therapeutic gardening groups make it both a public park and a working neighbourhood garden.
places.descriptionIt: Culpeper Community Garden occupa dal 1982 un terreno già destinato ad abitazioni vicino ad Angel. Prati e stagni comuni affiancano parcelle biologiche individuali, piantagioni per la fauna e un’area bambini; volontari, scuole e gruppi di ortoterapia lo rendono insieme parco pubblico e giardino di quartiere.

places.name: Dalston Eastern Curve Garden
places.description: Dalston Eastern Curve Garden follows the former Eastern Curve railway that once linked Dalston Junction with the North London Line. Opened as a community garden in 2010, it layers raised beds, trees, wildlife planting, greenhouse spaces and a café along the old track, with events and volunteer growing at its core.
places.descriptionIt: Dalston Eastern Curve Garden segue l’antica Eastern Curve ferroviaria che collegava Dalston Junction alla North London Line. Aperto come giardino comunitario nel 2010, dispone aiuole rialzate, alberi, piante per la fauna, serre e caffè lungo il vecchio tracciato, con eventi e coltivazioni volontarie al centro.

places.hookIt: Una curva ferroviaria dismessa è diventata il lungo e fitto giardino comunitario e luogo d’incontro di Dalston.

places.name: Danson Park
places.description: Danson Park surrounds an eighteenth-century mansion and long lake with broad lawns, woodland, wetland edges and boating, preserving the scale of a country estate inside suburban Bexleyheath.

places.name: Deen City Farm
places.description: Deen City Farm has brought animals, gardens and vocational learning to the River Wandle floodplain in Morden since 1978. Cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, poultry and horses support school visits and accredited training, while allotments, wetlands and community events connect the farm to its surrounding estates.

Bovini, pecore, capre, maiali, pollame e cavalli sostengono visite scolastiche e corsi riconosciuti; orti, zone umide ed eventi collegano la fattoria ai quartieri circostanti.

places.name: Dulwich Park
places.description: Dulwich Park opened in 1890 on former farmland and fields belonging to Dulwich College. Curving drives circle a boating lake, American Garden, winter garden, sports grounds and playgrounds; mature trees and restored Victorian features make the park a carefully composed counterpart to nearby Dulwich Picture Gallery.
places.descriptionIt: Dulwich Park aprì nel 1890 su campi appartenuti a Dulwich College. Viali curvi circondano lago navigabile, American Garden, giardino invernale, impianti sportivi e giochi; alberi maturi ed elementi vittoriani restaurati creano un paesaggio accurato vicino alla Dulwich Picture Gallery.

places.name: Eastcote House Gardens
places.description: Eastcote House Gardens preserve the grounds of a lost manor house beside the River Pinn. A Tudor dovecote, seventeenth-century coach house, walled garden, orchard, wildflower meadow and old trees survive around the house footprint, restored as a community heritage landscape.
places.descriptionIt: Eastcote House Gardens conserva i terreni di una dimora scomparsa lungo il fiume Pinn. Una colombaia Tudor, una rimessa seicentesca, giardino murato, frutteto, prato fiorito e alberi antichi circondano l’impronta della casa, restaurata come paesaggio storico comunitario.

places.name: Eden Dock
places.description: Eden Dock is a new waterside public realm in Canary Wharf designed to bring biodiversity back into the dock system. Floating wetlands, aquatic planting, boardwalks and seating create habitat for birds, insects and fish among the office towers, while visitors can move close to the water rather than viewing it only from quays.
places.descriptionIt: Eden Dock è un nuovo spazio pubblico sull’acqua a Canary Wharf, progettato per riportare biodiversità nel sistema dei docks. Zone umide galleggianti, piante acquatiche, passerelle e sedute creano habitat per uccelli, insetti e pesci tra le torri, permettendo ai visitatori di avvicinarsi all’acqua.

places.name: Eden Nature Garden
places.description: Eden Nature Garden was established in 2000 on disused church land beside St Paul’s Clapham. Volunteers use native planting, organic methods, ponds and habitat piles to support birds, insects and other wildlife, while the garden provides a quiet community space for play, learning and gardening.
places.descriptionIt: Eden Nature Garden fu fondato nel 2000 su un terreno ecclesiastico inutilizzato accanto a St Paul’s Clapham. I volontari impiegano specie autoctone, metodi biologici, stagni e rifugi naturali per sostenere uccelli e insetti, offrendo al quartiere uno spazio tranquillo per gioco, apprendimento e giardinaggio.

places.name: Epsom Downs Racecourse
places.description: Epsom Downs is open chalk grassland on the North Downs best known as the home of the Derby, first run here in 1780. Away from race meetings, public paths cross broad turf with long views toward London, while the racecourse grandstands and Tattenham Corner express the landscape’s sporting identity.
places.descriptionIt: Epsom Downs è un vasto prato calcareo dei North Downs, noto soprattutto come sede del Derby, disputato qui per la prima volta nel 1780. Fuori dalle giornate di corsa, sentieri pubblici attraversano l’erba con ampie vedute verso Londra; tribune e Tattenham Corner raccontano l’identità sportiva del paesaggio.

places.hookIt: Prati calcarei, vedute lontane di Londra e pista del Derby condividono un unico vasto paesaggio dei North Downs.

places.name: Freightliners Farm
places.description: Freightliners Farm grew from a 1970s community project that kept livestock in railway goods vans, giving the farm its name. Its Islington site now includes rare-breed animals, poultry, beehives, gardens and a café, with education and volunteering focused on farming, food and urban ecology.
places.descriptionIt: Freightliners Farm nacque da un progetto comunitario degli anni Settanta che ospitava animali in carri merci ferroviari, da cui deriva il nome. Il sito di Islington comprende oggi razze rare, pollame, alveari, orti e caffè, con educazione e volontariato dedicati ad agricoltura, cibo ed ecologia urbana.

places.name: Gibbons Rents secret garden
places.description: Gibbons Rent Community Garden occupies a narrow passage and former yard behind Bermondsey Street. Residents and local organisations transformed hard standing into raised beds, fruit trees, a greenhouse, children’s growing areas and sociable seating, creating a collectively tended shortcut between dense Southwark streets.
places.descriptionIt: Gibbons Rent Community Garden occupa un passaggio stretto e un antico cortile dietro Bermondsey Street. Abitanti e organizzazioni locali hanno trasformato il suolo duro in aiuole rialzate, alberi da frutto, serra, spazi di coltivazione per bambini e sedute, creando un collegamento verde curato collettivamente.

places.name: Gladstone Park
places.description: Gladstone Park spreads across the former Dollis Hill estate, where its high ground opens long views toward central London. Formal terraces near the surviving house stable block descend to sports pitches, playgrounds, mature avenues and the peaceful walled garden, with railway and wartime history around the edges.
places.descriptionIt: Gladstone Park si estende sull’antica tenuta di Dollis Hill, da cui si aprono lunghe vedute verso il centro di Londra. Terrazze formali presso le scuderie superstiti scendono verso campi sportivi, giochi, viali maturi e un tranquillo giardino murato, con tracce ferroviarie e belliche ai margini.

places.name: Greenwich Park
places.description: Greenwich Park rises from the National Maritime Museum to one of London’s defining panoramas beside the Royal Observatory. Its avenues, ancient trees, deer-park origins, flower and herb gardens, Roman remains and newly restored seventeenth-century landscape reveal layers of royal, scientific and social history.
places.descriptionIt: Greenwich Park sale dal National Maritime Museum fino a uno dei panorami più celebri di Londra, accanto al Royal Observatory. Viali, alberi secolari, origini come parco dei cervi, giardini fioriti ed erbari, resti romani e il paesaggio seicentesco restaurato raccontano una storia reale, scientifica e sociale stratificata.

places.name: Grovelands Park
places.description: Grovelands Park preserves the landscape around an eighteenth-century villa now used as a hospital. Humphry Repton advised on the estate design: a long lake, wooded slopes, grassland and veteran trees remain, joined today by sports courts, playgrounds and lakeside paths used by Winchmore Hill and Southgate communities.
places.descriptionIt: Grovelands Park conserva il paesaggio attorno a una villa settecentesca oggi utilizzata come ospedale. Humphry Repton contribuì al disegno della tenuta: restano un lungo lago, pendii boscosi, prati e alberi veterani, affiancati da campi sportivi, giochi e sentieri frequentati da Winchmore Hill e Southgate.

places.hookIt: Il parco influenzato da Repton scende tra alberi veterani e grandi prati verso un lungo lago ornamentale.

places.name: Gunnersbury Park
places.description: Gunnersbury Park is the former Rothschild estate shared by Ealing and Hounslow. Two mansions overlook lawns, lakes, an orangery, temple, Gothic ruins and historic gardens; museum galleries, sports facilities and continuing restoration reveal how an aristocratic landscape became a major public park.
places.descriptionIt: Gunnersbury Park è l’antica tenuta Rothschild condivisa da Ealing e Hounslow. Due ville dominano prati, laghi, aranciera, tempio, rovine gotiche e giardini storici; museo, impianti sportivi e restauri mostrano come un paesaggio aristocratico sia diventato un grande parco pubblico.

places.hookIt: Ville Rothschild, laghi ornamentali ed edifici da giardino definiscono una tenuta restaurata della Londra ovest.

places.name: Gunnersbury Triangle Nature Reserve
places.description: Gunnersbury Triangle is a six-acre nature reserve created on abandoned railway land between three active lines. Saved from development by a community campaign in the 1980s, its birch and willow woodland, ponds, meadow and acid grassland now shelter frogs, newts, butterflies and woodland birds.
places.descriptionIt: Gunnersbury Triangle è una riserva naturale di sei acri nata su terreno ferroviario abbandonato tra tre linee ancora attive. Salvata dallo sviluppo da una campagna locale negli anni Ottanta, ospita boschi di betulle e salici, stagni, prato e prateria acida con rane, tritoni, farfalle e uccelli.

places.hook: Community action turned an abandoned railway triangle into woodland, meadow and pond habitat.
places.hookIt: L’azione comunitaria ha trasformato un triangolo ferroviario abbandonato in habitat di bosco, prato e stagni.

places.name: Hackney City Farm
places.description: Hackney City Farm has occupied a former brewery and button-factory site off Hackney Road since 1984. Pigs, donkeys, goats, sheep and poultry share the compact grounds with gardens, pottery, classrooms and a café, supporting food education, volunteering and practical environmental projects.
places.descriptionIt: Hackney City Farm occupa dal 1984 il sito di un antico birrificio e fabbrica di bottoni vicino a Hackney Road. Maiali, asini, capre, pecore e pollame condividono gli spazi con orti, ceramica, aule e caffè, sostenendo educazione alimentare, volontariato e progetti ambientali pratici.

places.hook: Farm animals, food growing and craft workshops occupy an old industrial yard off Hackney Road.
places.hookIt: Animali, orti e laboratori artigianali occupano un antico cortile industriale vicino a Hackney Road.

places.name: Hampstead Heath
places.description: Hampstead Heath combines ancient woodland, rough grassland, swimming ponds and high viewpoints across 800 acres, offering a deliberately less formal landscape than London’s royal and municipal parks.
places.descriptionIt: Hampstead Heath unisce boschi antichi, prati irregolari, laghetti balneabili e punti panoramici su circa 800 acri, con un paesaggio volutamente meno formale dei parchi reali e comunali.
places.accessNotes: Visible from publicly accessible outdoor space. Visit considerately and respect residents, worshippers, wildlife and other users of the site.

places.name: Harleyford Road Community Garden
places.description: Harleyford Road Community Garden grew from wasteland left by demolished Georgian houses, where residents began cultivating vegetables in 1984. Its lawns, allotments, greenhouse, pond, play area, mosaic paths and mature trees form a volunteer-run buffer between nearby homes and the traffic of Harleyford Road.
places.descriptionIt: Harleyford Road Community Garden nacque su un terreno abbandonato dopo la demolizione di case georgiane, dove gli abitanti iniziarono a coltivare ortaggi nel 1984. Prati, parcelle, serra, stagno, area giochi, mosaici e alberi maturi creano una barriera gestita da volontari tra le case e il traffico di Harleyford Road.

places.hook: A resident-made garden of allotments, pond and mosaics occupies the footprint of demolished Georgian terraces.
places.hookIt: Un giardino creato dagli abitanti, con orti, stagno e mosaici, occupa l’area di terrazze georgiane demolite.

places.name: Horniman Gardens
places.description: Horniman Gardens spread across sixteen acres around the museum, with broad views toward central London. A sunken garden follows the Arts and Crafts design of 1912, while a medicinal garden, prairie planting, nature trail, musical installations and animal walk extend the museum’s themes outdoors.
places.descriptionIt: Gli Horniman Gardens si estendono per sedici acri intorno al museo, con ampie vedute verso il centro di Londra. Un giardino ribassato riprende il disegno Arts and Crafts del 1912; giardino medicinale, prateria, percorso naturalistico, installazioni musicali e recinto degli animali portano all’aperto i temi del museo.

places.hookIt: Aiuole Arts and Crafts, piante medicinali, animali e vedute dello skyline prolungano all’aperto l’Horniman Museum.

places.name: Hounslow Urban Farm
places.description: Hounslow Urban Farm occupies twenty-nine acres near Heathrow and grew from the former borough farm of the 1970s. Visitors meet farm animals, owls, reptiles and other species through scheduled demonstrations and handling sessions, making this a ticketed family attraction rather than an open public park.
places.descriptionIt: Hounslow Urban Farm occupa ventinove acri vicino a Heathrow e deriva dall’antica fattoria comunale degli anni Settanta. I visitatori incontrano animali da fattoria, gufi, rettili e altre specie durante dimostrazioni e attività guidate: è quindi un’attrazione familiare a pagamento, non un parco pubblico aperto.

places.hook: Farm livestock, owls and reptile encounters make this Heathrow-side site a hands-on ticketed attraction.
places.hookIt: Animali da fattoria, gufi e incontri con rettili rendono questo sito vicino a Heathrow un’attrazione pratica a pagamento.

places.name: Isabella Plantation
places.description: Isabella Plantation is a forty-acre woodland garden enclosed within Richmond Park and developed chiefly from the 1950s. Evergreen azaleas and rhododendrons blaze around streams and ponds in spring, while native woodland, bog planting and the accessible Broomfield Hill route sustain interest and wildlife year-round.
places.descriptionIt: Isabella Plantation è un giardino boschivo di quaranta acri dentro Richmond Park, sviluppato soprattutto dagli anni Cinquanta. Azalee sempreverdi e rododendri colorano ruscelli e stagni in primavera; bosco autoctono, piante di palude e percorso accessibile da Broomfield Hill mantengono interesse e biodiversità tutto l’anno.

places.hook: Spring azaleas and rhododendrons surround streams and ponds in Richmond Park’s enclosed woodland garden.
places.hookIt: Azalee e rododendri primaverili circondano ruscelli e stagni nel giardino boschivo recintato di Richmond Park.

places.name: Italian Gardens
places.description: The Italian Gardens form a formal Victorian water garden at the north end of Kensington Gardens. Four Carrara-marble basins, carved stonework, fountains and a richly planted pump house were created in the 1860s, probably as a gift from Prince Albert to Queen Victoria.
places.descriptionIt: Gli Italian Gardens sono un giardino d’acqua formale vittoriano all’estremità nord di Kensington Gardens. Quattro vasche in marmo di Carrara, sculture in pietra, fontane e una sala pompe riccamente decorata furono realizzati negli anni 1860, probabilmente come dono del principe Alberto alla regina Vittoria.

places.hook: Four marble fountain basins and an ornate pump house create Kensington Gardens’ most theatrical Victorian composition.
places.hookIt: Quattro vasche con fontane e una sala pompe ornata compongono la scenografia vittoriana più teatrale di Kensington Gardens.

places.name: Joseph Grimaldi Park
places.description: Joseph Grimaldi Park occupies the former burial ground of St James’s Chapel in Pentonville and is named for the celebrated clown buried here in 1837. Two coffin-shaped musical artworks chime when stepped on, while restored monuments, lawns and play space keep the unusual theatrical history visible.
places.descriptionIt: Joseph Grimaldi Park occupa l’antico cimitero della St James’s Chapel a Pentonville ed è intitolato al celebre clown sepolto qui nel 1837. Due opere musicali a forma di bara suonano quando vengono calpestate; monumenti restaurati, prati e giochi mantengono visibile questa insolita storia teatrale.

places.hook: Musical coffin sculptures and restored graves recall clown Joseph Grimaldi in a former chapel burial ground.
places.hookIt: Sculture musicali a forma di bara e tombe restaurate ricordano il clown Joseph Grimaldi in un antico cimitero.

places.name: Jubilee Park
places.description: Jubilee Park is a roof garden above Canary Wharf Underground station, designed by landscape architect Jacques Wirtz. Curving paths pass dense clipped hedges, lawns, fountains and mature trees that conceal much of the surrounding glass-and-steel skyline, making the park an engineered green room over transport infrastructure.
places.descriptionIt: Jubilee Park è un giardino pensile sopra la stazione della metropolitana di Canary Wharf, progettato dal paesaggista Jacques Wirtz. Sentieri curvi attraversano siepi scolpite, prati, fontane e alberi maturi che nascondono gran parte dello skyline di vetro e acciaio, creando una stanza verde sopra le infrastrutture.

places.hookIt: Siepi curve, fontane e chiome mature di Wirtz formano un giardino pensile direttamente sopra la Jubilee line.

places.name: Kentish Town City Farm
places.description: Kentish Town City Farm was founded in 1972 on railway land beside Gospel Oak, making it the United Kingdom’s first city farm. Thirty-two acres include farm animals, riding facilities, gardens and wildlife habitat around old railway structures, with youth work, therapy and environmental education central to its mission.
places.descriptionIt: Kentish Town City Farm fu fondata nel 1972 su terreno ferroviario vicino a Gospel Oak, diventando la prima city farm del Regno Unito. Trentadue acri comprendono animali, strutture per equitazione, orti e habitat naturali attorno a manufatti ferroviari, con lavoro giovanile, terapia ed educazione ambientale al centro.

places.hook: Britain’s first city farm combines railway heritage, riding, livestock and wildlife work beside Gospel Oak.
places.hookIt: La prima city farm britannica unisce patrimonio ferroviario, equitazione, animali e natura accanto a Gospel Oak.

places.name: Kyoto Garden
places.description: Kyoto Garden is a Japanese landscape garden within Holland Park, donated by the Kyoto Chamber of Commerce and opened in 1991. A tiered waterfall feeds a koi pond crossed by stone paths, with Japanese maples, clipped shrubs, lanterns and carefully placed rocks creating controlled seasonal views.
places.descriptionIt: Kyoto Garden è un giardino paesaggistico giapponese dentro Holland Park, donato dalla Camera di Commercio di Kyoto e aperto nel 1991. Una cascata a terrazze alimenta uno stagno con carpe koi; sentieri in pietra, aceri giapponesi, arbusti potati, lanterne e rocce compongono vedute stagionali controllate.

places.hookIt: Cascata, stagno con koi, aceri e lanterne di pietra compongono un dono di Kyoto dentro Holland Park.

places.name: Lesnes Abbey Woods
places.description: Lesnes Abbey Woods combine ancient woodland with the standing ruins of an Augustinian abbey founded in 1178. Paths cross coppiced hornbeam, heath and fossil-rich ground above the Thames marshes, while the excavated monastic plan, reconstructed cloister garden and panoramic viewpoints connect natural and archaeological history.
places.descriptionIt: Lesnes Abbey Woods unisce un bosco antico alle rovine di un’abbazia agostiniana fondata nel 1178. Sentieri attraversano carpini cedui, brughiera e terreni ricchi di fossili sopra le paludi del Tamigi; pianta monastica scavata, chiostro ricostruito e belvedere collegano natura e archeologia.

places.hookIt: Boschi antichi di carpino circondano un’abbazia del XII secolo e pendii fossiliferi sopra il Tamigi.

places.name: Lincoln’s Inn Fields
places.description: London’s largest public square is framed by legal chambers, Sir John Soane’s Museum and historic terraces; mature trees and open lawns create a calm civic garden between Holborn and the West End.

places.description: A broad green corridor through Hackney combines mature plane trees, sports, playgrounds and the heated lido, becoming especially lively when Broadway Market and summer gatherings spill into the park.

places.name: London Fields Lido
places.description: London Fields Lido is a heated, fifty-metre outdoor pool opened in 1932 at the edge of London Fields. Restored after a long closure, it offers lane swimming year-round with a sun terrace and changing facilities; this is a ticketed sports venue rather than a general park lawn.
places.descriptionIt: London Fields Lido è una piscina scoperta riscaldata di cinquanta metri, aperta nel 1932 ai margini di London Fields. Restaurata dopo una lunga chiusura, offre nuoto in corsia tutto l’anno con terrazza solarium e spogliatoi; è un impianto sportivo a pagamento, non un prato pubblico del parco.

places.hookIt: Un lido riscaldato degli anni Trenta, restaurato, offre nuoto tutto l’anno su cinquanta metri accanto a London Fields.

places.name: Marchmont Community Garden
places.description: Marchmont Community Garden opened in 2011 after residents, housing groups, Camden and the London Wildlife Trust reshaped an underused green. A serpentine path crosses lawn, perennial borders and surviving plane trees, with seating and wildlife-friendly planting designed for everyday use by Bloomsbury neighbours.
places.descriptionIt: Marchmont Community Garden aprì nel 2011 dopo che abitanti, associazioni, Camden e London Wildlife Trust riqualificarono uno spazio sottoutilizzato. Un sentiero sinuoso attraversa prato, bordure perenni e platani storici, con sedute e piante favorevoli alla fauna pensate per l’uso quotidiano del quartiere.

places.description: A landscaped valley park in Charlton contains a free council-run animal enclosure with deer, goats, pigs and poultry, combined with woodland, grassland and a section of the Green Chain Walk.

places.name: Mayfield Lavender Farm
places.description: Mayfield Lavender is a commercial lavender farm on the North Downs at Banstead, immediately beyond Greater London’s boundary. Rows of purple flowers cover the chalk soil in midsummer and supply lavender products, but flowering dates, photography rules, admission and opening are seasonal rather than park-like.
places.descriptionIt: Mayfield Lavender è un’azienda agricola di lavanda sui North Downs a Banstead, appena oltre il confine della Greater London. File di fiori viola coprono il suolo calcareo in piena estate e alimentano la produzione; fioritura, regole fotografiche, ingresso e apertura sono stagionali, non quelli di un normale parco.

places.hook: Midsummer rows of lavender cover a working chalk-land farm just beyond London’s southern boundary.
places.hookIt: File di lavanda estiva coprono una fattoria su suolo calcareo appena oltre il confine meridionale di Londra.

places.name: Morden Hall Park
places.description: Morden Hall Park follows the River Wandle through a former country estate, with wetland meadows, old parkland trees and several historic mill channels. An eighteenth-century snuff mill, white bridge, rose garden and surviving estate buildings explain how water, industry and leisure shaped this green stretch of south London.
places.descriptionIt: Morden Hall Park segue il fiume Wandle attraverso un’antica tenuta, con prati umidi, alberi secolari e canali storici dei mulini. Un mulino da tabacco del Settecento, il ponte bianco, il roseto e gli edifici della proprietà mostrano come acqua, industria e svago abbiano modellato questa parte verde di Londra sud.

places.hook: Wandle channels, wetlands and an old snuff mill weave through a country estate absorbed by south London.
places.hookIt: Canali del Wandle, zone umide e un antico mulino da tabacco attraversano una tenuta inglobata nella Londra sud.

places.name: Mudchute Park and Farm
places.description: Mudchute Park and Farm covers thirty-two acres on the Isle of Dogs, much of it formed from soil excavated during construction of the Millwall Dock. One of Europe’s largest urban farms, it combines livestock fields, horse riding, rare breeds, allotments and wartime anti-aircraft remains beneath views of Canary Wharf.
places.descriptionIt: Mudchute Park and Farm copre trentadue acri nell’Isle of Dogs, in gran parte formati dalla terra scavata durante la costruzione del Millwall Dock. Tra le più grandi fattorie urbane d’Europa, unisce pascoli, equitazione, razze rare, orti e resti antiaerei bellici sotto lo skyline di Canary Wharf.

places.hook: Thirty-two acres of livestock pasture and wartime traces sit beneath the towers of Canary Wharf.
places.hookIt: Trentadue acri di pascoli e tracce belliche si estendono sotto le torri di Canary Wharf.

places.name: Olden Community Garden
places.description: Olden Community Garden is a volunteer-run, two-acre nature site on Islington Council land near Highbury. Woodland, meadow, pond, orchard, vegetable beds and a children’s play area support local wildlife and community gardening, with public access concentrated around volunteer sessions and open days.
places.descriptionIt: Olden Community Garden è un’area naturalistica di due acri gestita da volontari su terreno del Comune di Islington, vicino a Highbury. Bosco, prato, stagno, frutteto, orti e area giochi sostengono fauna e giardinaggio comunitario; l’accesso pubblico si concentra durante turni di volontariato e giornate aperte.
places.accessNotes: This site is not an unrestricted public park: access is limited, event-led or by prior arrangement. Check the recorded source and confirm access before making a special journey.

places.hook: Two acres of woodland, meadow, orchard and pond are cared for collectively behind a Highbury gate.
places.hookIt: Due acri di bosco, prato, frutteto e stagno sono curati collettivamente dietro un cancello di Highbury.

places.name: Onion Garden
places.description: The Onion Garden transformed a narrow concrete service yard near Victoria Street into a dense container garden, café and inclusive community hub from 2021. Its layered planting, greenhouse, beehive and events demonstrated what could grow above Tube lines, but the Seaforth Place site closed after its lease ended in 2026.
places.descriptionIt: The Onion Garden trasformò dal 2021 uno stretto cortile cementato vicino a Victoria Street in un fitto giardino in vaso, caffè e centro comunitario inclusivo. Piante stratificate, serra, alveare ed eventi mostrarono cosa poteva crescere sopra le linee della metropolitana, ma il sito di Seaforth Place ha chiuso nel 2026 alla fine della concessione.

places.name: Osterley Park and House
places.description: Osterley Park is an eighteenth-century country estate surrounded by farmland and parkland now enclosed by west London. Robert Adam transformed the Tudor house for the Child banking family, while the grounds combine lakes, grand approaches, formal gardens, meadows and a working kitchen garden.
places.descriptionIt: Osterley Park è una tenuta settecentesca circondata da campi e parco, oggi inglobata nella Londra occidentale. Robert Adam trasformò la casa Tudor per la famiglia di banchieri Child; i terreni comprendono laghi, viali monumentali, giardini formali, prati e un orto produttivo.

places.hook: Robert Adam’s showpiece mansion sits within lakes, meadows and farmland unexpectedly enclosed by west London.
places.hookIt: La dimora scenografica di Robert Adam sorge tra laghi, prati e campi sorprendentemente inglobati nella Londra occidentale.

places.name: Oxleas Wood
places.description: Oxleas is part of an ancient woodland complex on Shooters Hill, with oak, hornbeam and hazel paths joining meadows, Severndroog Castle and the Green Chain Walk across unusually wild southeast-London ground.
places.descriptionIt: Oxleas fa parte di un antico complesso boschivo su Shooters Hill, dove sentieri tra querce, carpini e noccioli uniscono prati, Severndroog Castle e Green Chain Walk in un paesaggio insolitamente selvatico.

places.name: Pitch and Putt
places.description: Queen’s Park Pitch and Putt is a compact nine-hole, par-27 public course behind the park’s tennis courts. Club and ball hire are included in the fee, making it an informal introduction to golf, but opening hours depend on season, weather and daylight and admission is charged.
places.descriptionIt: Il Pitch and Putt di Queen’s Park è un compatto percorso pubblico di nove buche, par 27, dietro i campi da tennis. Noleggio di mazze e palline è compreso nel prezzo, offrendo un’introduzione informale al golf; orari dipendono però da stagione, meteo e luce e l’ingresso è a pagamento.

places.hookIt: Un percorso pubblico di nove buche offre golf informale dietro i campi da tennis di Queen’s Park, con attrezzatura inclusa.

places.name: Primrose Gardens
places.description: Primrose Gardens is a pair of small railed gardens laid out between the stucco terraces of Belsize Park. Formerly called Stanley Gardens, the plots were acquired by Hampstead Borough Council in 1920 and renamed in 1939; lawns, mature trees and central seating preserve the intimate scale of the Victorian street.
places.descriptionIt: Primrose Gardens è formato da due piccoli giardini recintati tra le terrazze in stucco di Belsize Park. Già chiamati Stanley Gardens, furono acquistati dal Comune di Hampstead nel 1920 e ribattezzati nel 1939; prati, alberi maturi e sedute centrali conservano la scala raccolta della strada vittoriana.

places.hook: Two pocket lawns and mature trees soften a short, architecturally unified Belsize Park terrace.
places.hookIt: Due piccoli prati e alberi maturi addolciscono una breve terrazza architettonicamente uniforme di Belsize Park.

places.name: Queen Mary's Rose Gardens
places.description: Queen Mary’s Gardens are the horticultural centrepiece of Regent’s Park, laid out in the former grounds of the Royal Botanic Society. Around 12,000 roses from hundreds of varieties surround formal beds, a lake, Mediterranean borders and the secluded St John’s Lodge Garden, with the strongest display in early summer.
places.descriptionIt: Queen Mary’s Gardens è il cuore orticolo di Regent’s Park, realizzato negli antichi terreni della Royal Botanic Society. Circa 12.000 rose di centinaia di varietà circondano aiuole formali, un lago, bordure mediterranee e il raccolto St John’s Lodge Garden, con il massimo splendore all’inizio dell’estate.

places.hookIt: La grande collezione di rose di Regent’s Park circonda aiuole formali, un lago e raccolte stanze verdi.

places.name: Queen’s Wood
places.description: Queen’s Wood preserves ancient hornbeam and oak woodland on steep ground between Highgate and Muswell Hill, with winding paths, seasonal wildflowers and a community café in a former keeper’s lodge.
places.descriptionIt: Queen’s Wood conserva un antico bosco di carpini e querce sui pendii tra Highgate e Muswell Hill, con sentieri sinuosi, fiori stagionali e un caffè comunitario nell’ex casa del guardiano.

places.name: Red Cross Garden
places.description: Red Cross Garden was created in 1887 by social reformer Octavia Hill as the green heart of an experimental housing scheme for local workers. Restored Arts and Crafts cottages face lawns, flower borders, a pond and the community hall, expressing Hill’s belief that beauty and open space belonged in everyday urban life.
places.descriptionIt: Red Cross Garden fu creato nel 1887 dalla riformatrice sociale Octavia Hill come cuore verde di un complesso abitativo sperimentale per lavoratori. Cottage Arts and Crafts restaurati guardano prati, bordure fiorite, stagno e sala comunitaria, esprimendo l’idea di Hill che bellezza e spazio aperto appartenessero alla vita urbana quotidiana.

places.hookIt: Cottage, stagno e aiuole di Octavia Hill uniscono riforma dell’edilizia sociale e disegno Arts and Crafts.

places.name: Richmond Park
places.description: Richmond Park is London’s largest Royal Park and a National Nature Reserve, enclosed as a royal hunting ground in the seventeenth century. Free-roaming red and fallow deer share acid grassland, ancient oaks and ponds; King Henry’s Mound protects a celebrated sightline to St Paul’s Cathedral.
places.descriptionIt: Richmond Park è il più grande Royal Park di Londra e una riserva naturale nazionale, recintato nel Seicento come riserva di caccia reale. Cervi rossi e daini liberi condividono praterie acide, querce antiche e stagni; King Henry’s Mound tutela una celebre visuale verso St Paul’s Cathedral.

places.hookIt: Cervi liberi, querce antiche e vedute protette rendono Richmond Park un paesaggio urbano di importanza nazionale.

places.name: Royal Botanic Gardens
places.description: The Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew preserve one of the world’s most important living plant collections across a historic Thames-side landscape. The Palm House, Temperate House, Princess of Wales Conservatory, arboretum and scientific collections trace plant diversity, conservation and botanical exchange over more than 250 years.
places.descriptionIt: I Royal Botanic Gardens di Kew custodiscono una delle più importanti collezioni botaniche viventi al mondo in un paesaggio storico lungo il Tamigi. Palm House, Temperate House, Princess of Wales Conservatory, arboreto e collezioni scientifiche raccontano oltre 250 anni di biodiversità, conservazione e scambi botanici.
